js.comment: Saved-Tabs Tier-2 DRIVE orchestrator (SW half, spec [ap:7S217K] §6/§8; U01 per contract [ap:08ZEAO]): strictly sequential (A5/G6) — per entry: STEP 0 the configurable inter-tab delay (saved_tabs_drive_delay_seconds re-read per gap via loadExtensionSettings — a mid-drive change takes effect at the next tab; interruptible; never before this drive's first create), the cancel check (a stopped drive reports this and every remaining entry skipped-cancelled, then the summary), STEP 3 create at PLAIN https://workflowy.com/ (SAVED_TABS_DRIVE_TAB_URL — the entry's saved page url is IGNORED since U02 [ap:DLGU66]; no url admission, no entry ever fails over its url) — REUSING the previous drive's window when it still exists (savedTabsDriveLastWindowId via chrome.windows.get; otherwise ONE new window: first entry chrome.windows.create unfocused, later entries chrome.tabs.create in that window, active:false — G1/D5 rev-2 as amended; a failed create unbinds and the next entry re-resolves), STEP 4 await THAT tab's endpoint_register observation via pendingTabReadiness RACED against the drive's cancel signal (the ONE hook in the frame-inspection branch — never a timer/poll, G2/D2; the caps are liveness hygiene; a stop tears the waiter down and reports the entry failed with a cancelled reason — its tab stays open), deliver alias+spec in ONE saved_tabs_drive_apply frame via sendToTab (spec by object identity — A1/G4), STEP 6 await the correlated saved_tabs_drive_apply_response raced against the cancel signal the same way; a failing entry never aborts the rest (D7 — every failure named with phase+reason); progress frames per transition to the ORIGIN tab (D4; origin death now STOPS the drive at once via stopSavedTabsDrive — cancellation semantics, D8 amended); a delaying progress frame announces each inter-tab gap; terminal summary (G7/G8), then singleton + eviction marker cleared; entered via the saved_tabs_drive_request branch (handleSavedTabsDriveRequest — acceptance ack; a concurrent request SUPERSEDES the running drive instead of being refused); extension-INTERNAL kinds only — never the broker wire (A2)

Raised from 12s to 30s (Dan) because a genuinely large server render can legitimately exceed 12s. DISTINCT from: the push path's generous 180000ms leak-cap (a ~minute-long render is decoupled from the MCP ack), and MODAL_KEEPALIVE_MS=12000 (the SW keepalive, which MUST stay < ~30s MV3 idle-eviction and is NOT a reply timeout).

Aug-2026 DE-STORAGE: formerly sessionStorage-backed (key glimpse_modal_state) so the knobs survived a full page reload; Dan's explicit decision made that reload-persistence unwanted (a refresh SHOULD reset the dock -- you re-Apply the slice and retype any since/item-count override; slice groups now carry their own stored default SORT (SGSORT, 2026), so Apply seeds the sort knob for free via the server render_scope echo -- the `since` feature is fully implemented but has no per-group stored default, so an item-count/window override is retyped per render), so the backing is now a plain module var that dies with the page. Function names/signatures UNCHANGED so every getMdPreview*/setTabModalState call site is unaffected; still per-page-context (per-tab), still the SOLE authority the accessors read; ribbon widgets write on user edit, adoptRenderScope writes on a successful server render echo. THE single monotonic RENDER-GENERATION counter for the docked modal -- the keystone of the dock's async-render supersession model. A new render INTENT (a genuine selection change in setDockedSelection, a root-set/Refresh in prepareDockedServerRender, and -- as of the async dock-render-task refactor -- a slice APPLY/PUSH via displaySliceInDock) claims a fresh generation by ++dockedRenderGeneration; each async request captures the value it was fired under and acts ONLY if it still equals the current one at reply/paint time, so EVERY stale reply (success, failure, null, timeout) is dropped by ONE rule and a superseded render can never clobber a newer view. ONE shared clock governs BOTH the DOM-render path and the slice/push paint path (most-recent intent wins the paint chokepoint, independent of which async render finishes first). Historically unbeaconed, which hid it from the f8-expand/md-preview slice and led an architecture session to propose a NEW counter instead of extending this one; beaconed now so the next agent to touch async-render correctness sees it. NOTE: a bare top-level `let` is not symbol-addressable via read_text_snippet_by_symbol, so this block is also the read handle for the counter.

This is the DOM-capture twin of renderDockedMultiSelection, deliberately NOT a RenderProjectionSpec/dockedSliceContext path.

Browser-side string->HTML render entry for the docked Markdown modal: takes the canonical Python composer's Markdown STRING and renders it to HTML via marked.parse (safe prewrapped-plain fallback on a marked error). The server returns Markdown, NEVER HTML; this is the sole HTML-rendering step, shared by the live and frozen render paths. SOURCE-VIEW branch (Dan, 2026): when the dock's dockedSourceViewMode is 'source', the SAME string is painted as escaped plain text through the dockedSourceHtml <pre> choke (find-in-source highlights applied) instead of marked.parse -- a strictly client-side presentation toggle; NOTHING upstream of this function changes (no spec / render_scope / wire field). MATH (2026): inline $...$ and display $$...$$ render via KaTeX -- a small pandoc-flavored marked extension defined in marked-katex-init.js is registered on the global marked instance at content-script load (throwOnError:false), so THIS call site stays byte-unchanged.

Find-in-source query compiler for the dock Source view -- the HIGHLIGHT-only JS mini-twin of the server's build_search_predicate smart grammar (lightning_rod_search.py; twins-by-one-grammar, the SinceCodec-pair precedent). Tokenizes whitespace with "quoted phrase" support (unbalanced quote = loud {ok:false}), skips the OR/AND keywords and negated (- / !) terms (negation is meaningful for node FILTERING but not for highlight-in-place; ignored in v1), escapes every regex metacharacter then restores the * / ? GLOB wildcards, drops patterns that could match the empty string (a bare '*' would yield an infinite zero-length-match stream), and returns ONE combined case-insensitive alternation RegExp. Returns {ok:true, regex:null} for a blank/all-negated query (= clear highlights). Keep in lockstep with the server grammar's positive-term subset.

THE single <pre> paint choke for the dock's TEXT views: the Source-view branch of composedMarkdownToHtml AND the native raw_text content format (composedContentToHtml) both route through here. Escapes the composer string (escapeHtmlForPreview) and, when a find-in-source regex is armed, wraps every match in mark.glimpse-dock-src-hit (the FIRST match also gets the --current class), recording dockedSourceSearchCount/Current for the nav buttons. Re-runs on EVERY paint, so highlights re-apply automatically after row clicks / Refresh / Apply / push. SAME escapeHtmlForPreview + glimpse-md-preview-plain idiom the marked-failure fallback always used -- no new rendering path.

Instant LOCAL re-paint of the dock bottom pane from the held dockedRenderedSource through composedContentToHtml (current content_format honored) -- the Source/Rendered toggle's apply step and the find-in-source re-highlight step. NO server round trip, NO render-generation claim (synchronous; an in-flight reply that lands afterward paints through the current mode, correct by construction); preserves scrollTop. Cluster siblings: compileDockSourceSearch / dockedSourceHtml / applyDockSourceSearch / navigateDockSourceSearch / refreshDockSourceSearchUi.

The ONE dock toast lifecycle authority. Replaces/starts the transient top-center toast; manual click dismissal clears the timer and leaves controls immediately usable, while automatic timeout dismissal alone arms a 1000ms capture-phase click shield over interactive dock controls. This prevents the toast-vanished-before-mouseup race from accidentally clicking Freeze/Sync behind it without using pointer-events:none (which would pass clicks through to Workflowy). New toast display clears any prior shield. Pure client UI state; no persistence.

The ONE place that converts a dock render/action reply into a user-facing failure, so every caller surfaces the server's actionable text identically instead of a bare 'ERR' flash or a silent blank. Distinguishes the three failure modes the endpoint-liveness work defined: res==null -> TRANSPORT failure (no reply / cold socket / timeout); res.code=='unknown_endpoint' -> endpoint-liveness GHOST (tab dropped on an MV3 SW reconnect, already asked to re-register in the background -> retry), preferring the server's own res.error; res.success!==true -> any other structured failure surfaced verbatim (fallback to the caller's fallbackMessage). Returns true iff a failure was surfaced (caller early-returns), false on a success to render. UI propagation ONLY: shows a toast, optionally paints the message into the supplied dock render element and clears the source/leaf-count -- it NEVER renders content and touches no protocol/routing/retry/broker behavior.
js.role: ƒ surfaceRenderFailure(res, opts): the single UI helper that turns a render/action reply into the right user-facing failure message

js.comment: Docked Markdown modal 'Copy ID' feature: copy a tree-view row's Workflowy SEARCH STRING `id:<uuid>` to the clipboard (via the shared navigator.clipboard->fallbackCopy path) and flash a showDockToast telling the user to paste it into Workflowy's search box to reveal the node. Invoked (toggle-gated on dockedCopyIdMode) from setDockedSelection so both click and arrow-key selection copy; the full search string is copied (not the bare UUID) so a single paste locates the node.

ONE shared client helper that builds the full render_spec blob for the dock's current cache-sourced view, merging dockedSliceContext.render_spec (the server-adopted scope) with the currently-selected row as spec.focus. Used by BOTH the get_current_modal_render_spec WS leaf query (render_spec='modal') and the '⌖ focus' copy button (fallback paste blob), so the two surfaces cannot drift. Pure in-memory state read; no rendering, no WS round-trip; the server re-projects through the Python composer.

This closes the old scope gap from the bare focus triple: the blob carries group_id/root_uuid/match_scope/etc. AND the focus field. Browser twin of the server's _slice_row_key. Cross-language contract point -- change both together.

Shared generated timeout policy for cache-backed row renders. Grows from the interactive floor using the already-known final row count, caps at the established 180s long-render ceiling, and never inspects opaque LensSpec atoms; socket-close cleanup remains the immediate failure detector.

Fire an occurrence-exact render_slice_row re-projection from the stored RenderProjectionSpec. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the on-the-wire lightning selection block carried on render_slice_modal / render_slice_row / apply_slice_in_dock frames. Emits the opaque per-mode selection, including render_lens{lens,query,query_mode,match_scope}; LensSpec is copied verbatim and never interpreted client-side. Used by requestSliceModalRender + requestSliceRowRender so Refresh, row focus, readback, and push cannot drop mode-specific fields.

Client-side SGSORT sort normalizer, the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec kind-aware sort rule. Requires kind to be known before sort coercion: null/omitted survives only for slice/slice_override request specs (inherit the group's saved default at the server resolve-point), raw_root/lightning collapse null to the explicit 'none' document-order sentinel, and the string 'none' remains distinct from null. Used by the spec builders and normalizeRenderScopeToSpec so Apply/push/request frames preserve the no-cracks null-vs-'none' boundary across the client wire.

CLIENT-side reconstruction of a RenderProjectionSpec from the SERVER's authoritative render_scope echo -- the single fan-in that makes the client half of the shared-object architecture work. adoptRenderScope calls this and stores the result as the SOLE field of dockedSliceContext (dockedSliceContext.render_spec), so the client Refresh (refreshDockedMarkdownPanel) and per-row re-render (requestSliceRowRender) reuse the EXACT scope the server just rendered -- kind / group_id / group_name / root_uuid / opaque lightning selection / match_scope / descend_policy / recursive ([ap:EPR86W] part a: the depth leg of the traversal pair; false = the scope root + its DIRECT children only, raw-root-only today) / sort / since / recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a): the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection; null = the server resolves it) / headings_only / content_format / tree_mode. This IS the client's scope handle: there are no separate scalar mirrors beside it. Derives kind from scope.kind, falling back to the (lightning|group_id+root_uuid|group_id|else) presence truth table for a partial/older scope; preserves the opaque lightning selection verbatim (never interprets it -- the server routes by selection.mode). Tolerant of missing fields (each falls back to RENDER_SPEC_DEFAULTS). This is the JS twin of the Python RenderProjectionSpec normalizers; the small make{Slice,RawRoot,Lightning}RenderSpec factories (used by the human Apply / Lightning ribbon spec-build sites) sit just above and ride under this block. descend_policy and recursive round-trip through here, so Refresh/per-row preserve them for free.

G3 liveness cleanup: settle EVERY in-flight render_slice_modal / render_slice_row promise on transport death (page-world BridgeSocket ws.onclose). Resolves each pending waiter with null -- the SAME 'render failed' signal the 180s leak-cap timeout and a cold-socket send use -- so the failure flows through the ONE existing G2 sink (the caller's `!res` branch: the push receiver's dock toast, the APPLY button's flash('ERR')) instead of hanging until a wall-clock timeout. GENERATION-AGNOSTIC by design: the transport is gone, so ALL pending renders are moot regardless of dockedRenderGeneration -- settle them all to avoid a promise/timer leak. NEVER-REJECT: resolve(null) (not reject) keeps the contract every caller already handles (a rejection would need new try/catch at each await site); the timers are cleared here so no stale resolve(null) fires later.

Fire a render_slice_modal WS request (the Apply-slice FULL-DOCUMENT render). SPEC-ONLY signature: the SOLE arg is a RenderProjectionSpec (+ an optional { renderTimeoutMs } opts bag); a non-spec 1st arg is a loud fail-fast (no positional fallback). The spec is unpacked at the top into the SAME locals the body uses -- group_id + this tab's endpoint_id are sent on the frame, and the spec's view fields drive the sort. SORT PRECEDENCE (now entirely spec-expressed): the spec's sort_by/sort_direction map onto the internal explicit-sortOverride branch, which ALWAYS wins over the internal forceDefaultSort (fixed false for a spec) and never reads/mutates the global md_preview_sort_* store -- so the agent/server push honors the GLIMPSE call's sort, and the human APPLY button expresses its 'default view' intent by BUILDING a spec with sort_by:'none'. The spec's `since` is forwarded verbatim ('' => no since on this render); the global dock since is never inherited here. The server RE-PROJECTS the slice from cache (build_stage1_base_tree) and returns the composed Markdown + tree-view rows + Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields; resolves with the reply dict or null on cold-socket/timeout. Rides the generic request_id rail (handleRenderSliceModalResult resolves render_slice_modal_result AND render_slice_row_result).

SHARED cache-scope apply orchestration: render any cache-projected scope into the docked modal through ONE RenderProjectionSpec path (requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> displaySliceInDock, forwarding Tier-2 live-GUI-sync fields when applicable). Handles slice groups (group_id), slice overrides (group_id + root_uuid), raw-root dumps (root_uuid only), anchor views (raw_root + descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors'), and Lightning Rod selections. The human slice APPLY button, anchor-view APPLY rows, and agent/server push all funnel through this one function. Sort/since/headings are EXPLICIT per-render args (never read from global dock state when supplied), and UI feedback is injected via optional hooks. Returns the server result (or null) so callers can branch on success.

Resolve the root UUID a Lightning Rod ribbon action should scope to = whatever the docked modal is CURRENTLY rooted at, regardless of provenance. SLICE mode (Apply/push/prior Lightning Rod) has dockedRootUuid=null, so read the adopted render_scope's root_uuid (dockedRenderScope || dockedSliceContext); DOM mode uses dockedRootUuid. Returns '' when neither is set (nothing displayed yet) so the caller shows the 'select a node first' toast. The Lightning Rod ribbon has NO paste-a-UUID field BY DESIGN -- it always acts on the current modal root.

SHARED render-into-dock tail for a Lightning Rod spec: requestSliceModalRender -> captureSinceFieldsFromResult -> surfaceRenderFailure -> displaySliceInDock with the standard group-less meta block (group_id:null, the lightning root, empty sync bundle). Extracted from triggerLightningRod's Global fork so the dynamic-slice-group dialog submit can reuse it byte-for-byte (STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: a duplicated pure block is the only Stage-0 crack).

Fire a Lightning Rod from the dock ribbon. mode is 'gather' | 'render_tags' | 'render_search'; the single text box feeds BOTH render modes (render_search verbatim as `query`, render_tags split on whitespace/commas into `tags`); matchScope ('name'|'name_and_note') rides inside the opaque lightning selection. Roots at resolveLightningRodRootUuid() (the current modal root; NO paste-a-UUID field). scoped (the 4th arg, ap:LRSCOPE/ap:LRHAND2) selects between TWO forks: (GLOBAL, scoped falsy) the original path -- build a kind='lightning_rod' RenderProjectionSpec and requestSliceModalRender -> displaySliceInDock, walking the WHOLE cache root; (SCOPED, scoped truthy) confine the search to the dock's CURRENT frozen artifact via requestScopedLightningDomCapture, producing an EPHEMERAL kind='dom_capture' result routed through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock (one-way door; the durable slice/raw origin is discarded, re-Apply to return). Scoped requires dockedFrozen; it sends the pinned captured tree (DOM-frozen) OR the durable base_render_spec + wasSlice (slice-frozen, server projects+filters), plus the optional occurrence-exact selected-row focus as the DOMAIN re-root pre-step (distinct from plain row-click navigation). Global is byte-for-byte the prior behavior.
js.role: async function triggerLightningRod(mode, query, matchScope, scoped)

js.comment: Trigger for the Dynamic Slice Group dialog. If exactly one row is selected, opens the dialog normally with that row as the root. If multiple rows are selected (or zero), opens the dialog with the main fields DISABLED — only the recent entries list is interactive, so the user can pick a recent definition to pre-populate and re-enable the fields.

Floating dialog for the Dynamic Slice Group feature. When row is non-null, the root UUID + name are shown as static text and all fields are enabled. When row is null (multi-select or no selection), the fields are DISABLED and only the recent entries list at the bottom is interactive — clicking a recent entry pre-populates the fields, updates the static root text, and re-enables everything. On Submit: builds a lightning {mode:'render_tags', tags, postfix_policy:'slice', match_scope} spec, saves the definition to localStorage (_saveDynSliceRecent), builds a RenderProjectionSpec via makeLightningRenderSpec, and delegates to _renderLightningSpecIntoDock. Esc = Cancel, Enter = Submit.

TIER-2 deferred-on-scroll live-GUI-sync watcher installed after an Apply-slice. Reissues the slice membership search, then fires each server pending expand/collapse op by UUID as its row materializes during natural reading-scroll (MutationObserver + scroll listener, rAF-coalesced). EXPAND fires freely (additive; recursive expandSubtreeSafeById -> cascade re-scan catches newly-materialized targets). COLLAPSE fires only when its gated_by expansion ancestors have ALL fired (asymmetric-merge gating; gated_by=[] fires freely). Full safety set after Sync starts: query-bound/tab-bound/keypress-disarm/new-slice-disarm/fire-once/getItemById-recheck/isExpanded-guard + configurable timeout (slice_watcher_timeout_seconds, default 30s, started by the Sync button -- NOT at Apply). While dormant before Sync, modal reading/navigation keypresses do NOT tear down the stored sync plan. Single global watcher; a new install tears down the prior one. Updates the dock status with a flashing GUI-sync countdown and a pending-ops remaining count.

THE single client-side fan-out for a server-echoed render_scope (Option Y, Dan's 'server is the one choke point' model). Called by displaySliceInDock on EVERY successful cache-projected render, regardless of which SURFACE triggered it (a ribbon-widget click -> usually a no-op adopt of the client's own values; an MCP glimpse(push_to_modal=true) call -> a real update that lights up the ribbon). It (1) stores the whole scope in dockedRenderScope (footer display source), (2) mirrors scope IDENTITY into dockedSliceContext (the re-render/per-row scope handle: group_id + root_uuid), and (3) mirrors the VIEW params (sort_by/sort_direction/since/headings_only) into the per-tab render state via setTabModalState so the ribbon widgets + since field repaint to match. Adoption is fail-closed for invalid server-echo `since`: the scope is decoded before any state mutation, and a malformed/string wire value surfaces through the yellow bar and aborts adoption, preserving last-known-good state. Otherwise the since field's existing draft guard (refreshSinceHeadingsUi skips overwriting sinceInput while it is focused) is preserved so a reply landing mid-type never stomps the user's keystrokes. Pure UI/state fan-out; no I/O, no server round-trip.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD (ap:LRSCOPE) EPHEMERAL display path — the destination of the crack-closer branch in displaySliceInDock for a kind='dom_capture' render_scope. It does NOT adoptRenderScope / normalizeRenderScopeToSpec / set dockedSliceContext.render_spec (that is exactly the launder the crack-closer prevents). Instead it RE-PINS the server-filtered forest as the dock's FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE captured tree (dockedRenderSource='dom', dockedFrozen=true, dockedFrozenSingleActive=true, dockedFrozenSingleTree/Rows set from meta.filtered_forest/rows), so EVERY downstream operation (per-row single render, sort/since via refreshFrozenDomAfterViewChange, frozenDomCapturedTree, resolveLightningRodRootUuid's DOM branch) is handled by the EXISTING frozen-DOM machinery with NO new per-consumer branching. This is the Lightning-within-Lightning wholesale forest replacement: the next Scoped run filters THIS pinned forest. Paints row 0's markdown immediately (raw_text for a gather outline, else marked); suppresses the scroll warning (complete by construction). Ephemeral by construction — nothing durable is stored, so it can never be Refreshed/re-projected as a cache scope.

Display an Apply-slice server render in the dock as a standalone, cache-sourced, inherently-FROZEN document. Sets render PROVENANCE to 'slice' (+ dockedSliceContext={group_id,group_name} so a SLICE-mode Refresh re-applies the same slice), force-FREEZES (dockedRootUuid stays null -- a slice is NOT a DOM view, so live Workflowy clicks must not re-walk it), and POPULATES the top-half tree-view from the server's ordered rows (each carrying the (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) identity triple) instead of blanking it. Records the slice render mode -- 'snapshot' (server pre-rendered every row's option-Y view, kept in dockedSliceSnapshot keyed by sliceRowKey -> instant row clicks) or 'single' (large slice -> requestSliceRowRender on demand). Paints the full-document markdown (row 0's view) immediately, selects row 0 without re-rendering, and SUPPRESSES the scroll warning (cache_sourced; wired through selectionProvablyComplete). Sets dockedPaneHasGoodContent + the rendered source for char-count/Copy-MD.

Resolve the pending merge_slice_groups promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the full merge report (root, tag counts, Q4 mutation ledger, verification block, persistence record) from the server handler.

Q4 Lightning Rod batch tag-mutation wire helper (the section-9 wire contract). CALLED BY _submitTagMutation (the dock 🏷️ Tags… popup submit) -- the older "NO UI affordance calls this yet" note is stale. Fire a mutate_node_tags WS request {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, operations:[{handle, operation:'add'|'remove', tags:[...]} | {handle, operation:'rename', old_tag, new_tag}]} (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server's mutate_node_tags_result ledger, or null on cold-socket/timeout. OWN 180s timeout class (a batch runs tens of seconds) -- deliberately NOT the shared 30s INTERACTIVE_WS_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS. Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders (G3). The server handler runs the SAME WorkflowyTagMutationSpec.from_wire grammar core + _lightning_rod_mutate_tags orchestrator as the MCP boundary. The dock already has everything a future UI needs to harvest handles: occurrence-exact row UUID triples + multi-select (dockedSelectedIndices / handleDockRowClick / updateDockRowMarkers).

Resolve the pending anchor_dock_update promise keyed on request_id (the handleMutateNodeTagsResult analog). The reply carries the canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl result (success, no_op, favorite, local, attributes, families_updated, tags, warnings) or a structured error (error_code + extra for dock_families_ambiguous).

Fire an anchor_dock_update WS request (the section-9 wire contract) and resolve with the server's anchor_dock_update_result, or null on cold-socket/timeout. Carries INTENT ONLY: {action, request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, dock_handle, favorite?|local?, families?}. The client composes NO tag, resolves NO handle, picks NO postfix word. OWN pending map (pendingAnchorDockUpdate) + the shared 30s interactive timeout class; socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. The server handler runs AnchorDockUpdateSpec.from_wire (transport shell only) + the ONE canonical _anchor_dock_update_impl seam the MCP anchor.dock.update tool uses.

THE ONE client-side group-refs normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_group_refs in merge_slice_groups_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks: groups is a list of 2+ items; STRING items are named groups (id-or-name); OBJECT items are dynamic definitions with root_uuid + tags ('#'-stripped, de-duped, '--' postfix tails rejected). Returns {groups, error} — never throws. The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine).
Mint the normalized client-side merge spec object (the JS twin of MergeSliceGroupsSpec). { groups, mode, tag } — frozen-by-convention. Consumed by requestMergeSliceGroups.

THE wire helper for merge_slice_groups (the requestMutateNodeTags analog). Sends {action:'merge_slice_groups', request_id, endpoint_id, v:1, groups, mode, tag} with CANONICAL group refs (named = bare string; dynamic = {root_uuid, tags}) -- the Python _normalize_group_refs grammar, NOT the internal normalized refs. Timeout: args.timeout_seconds (an optional caller-declared wait deadline, e.g. set near a UI button) rides the frame as INTERIM transport metadata (NOT a spec field; REMOVED on the async-CARTO-job migration); fallback = conservative estimate (2.0 s x groups.length*20, 30 s floor; the true A8 value is server-side). Socket-drop settling rides failAllPendingSliceRenders. NO client-side persistence (A9): the server handler persists via create_slice_group; the reply carries the persistence record. NO UI affordance calls this in v1 (exactly how requestMutateNodeTags shipped).

THE ONE client-side operations-grammar normalizer (the JS twin of Python _normalize_operations in lightning_rod_tag_mutation_spec.py). Mirrors the Python checks 1:1: non-empty list, per-verb allowed fields, handle required, duplicate handles rejected, add/remove need tags, rename needs old_tag+new_tag. Returns {operations, error} — never throws. Consumed by makeTagMutationSpec + buildTagMutationSpecFromDockSelection (the dock funnel). The server's from_wire remains the authoritative boundary; this is the client pre-flight twin (dual-normalizer doctrine, same as the render-spec precedent).

The async submit handler for the dock-UI batch tag mutation popup. Fires the shipped requestMutateNodeTags wire helper (the section-9 frame, 180s timeout class), surfaces the result as a toast (committed/noop/failed or batch-abort error) + console ledger, and runs a provenance-aware post-mutation refresh: SLICE provenance auto-Refresh via refreshDockedMarkdownPanel (the server eagerly patches the /nodes-export cache, so the re-projection reflects tag changes including membership/policy effects); frozen-DOM provenance toasts a pinned-view note (does NOT fake freshness). This is the ONE place the mutate_node_tags wire round-trip meets the dock UI.

Client half of the UUID Explorer List anchors round-trip: mints request_id + endpoint_id, sends action=list_anchors_for_widget (with tree_view / show_local_anchors / include_raw_text / favorites_only flags), and resolves the correlated list_anchors_for_widget_result. Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch; the server owns anchor enumeration. favorites_only rides beside show_local_anchors; the server treats an absent/false flag as the full inventory, so the Saved-Tabs Dock picker (which omits it) keeps seeing every Dock while the Anchors popup sends true for the favorites shortlist.

Fire a render_lightning_dom_capture WS request (the client half of the Scoped Lightning Rod). Mirrors requestCompileSliceSearch's small self-contained round-trip (client-minted request_id, this tab's endpoint_id, ensureSocketReady, 12s timeout, single pending map pendingScopedLightning). Sends ONE of two payload shapes: DOM-frozen carries capturedTree (the pinned frozen forest from frozenDomCapturedTree().tree); slice-frozen carries baseRenderSpec (the durable dockedSliceContext.render_spec) + wasSlice=true and NO capturedTree, so the server projects the base slice to a tree then filters it. Forwards the opaque lightning selection, the optional occurrence-exact row focus (for the domain re-root pre-step), and the dock's current view knobs (as_markdown/headings_only/sort_by/sort_direction/since). Resolves with the reply dict (kind='dom_capture' ephemeral artifact) or null on cold-socket/timeout; the caller routes it through displaySliceInDock -> the crack-closer -> displayScopedDomCaptureInDock.

Defensive collapse helper for the F8 plan: resolves a UUID to a WF item and calls WF.collapseItem(item) if that API exists, else logs a loud console error and returns false (no silent no-op). Counterpart to expandSubtreeSafeById; collapsing a topmost target hides its whole subtree in one call.

Mechanically apply a server F8 plan to the live DOM: expand (via expandSubtreeSafeById) FIRST, then collapse_suppressed then collapse_deprecated (via collapseSubtreeRootById), in that order. Expand-first so a contraction nested inside an expansion region survives (expanding first then collapsing the pocket sticks; the reverse would re-open it). Pure realizer of the returned UUID sets; no client-side policy. Logs any plan warnings.

Build an F8 node's NAME string with its tags guaranteed space-separated and '#'-prefixed, by harvesting .contentTag data-val (the authoritative tag source rowHasNexusExpandTag uses) and appending them to the plain base text. Fixes the textContent tag-gluing bug where server-side extract_name_tags lost glued/'#'-less tags and F8 returned expand=0.

In-place post-pass over an extractSearchResults/extractChildren tree: for each node, look up its live DOM element by projectid and replace its name with extractNodeNameWithTagsForF8(el) so glued/'#'-less tags survive into the server's extract_name_tags. Structure (ids, parent nesting) is left exactly as the proven extractor produced it.

F8 visible-DOM serializer. Delegates to the proven GLIMPSE extraction (extractSearchResults under active search, else extractChildren) rooted like extractDOMTree, so parent nesting is CANONICAL and matches the /nodes-export cache even in search mode (fixes the rootId=None 'Home' + edge-mismatch bug). Then runs retagF8TreeNames so the server's extract_name_tags sees tag-faithful names. Returns {success, root:{id,name,note}, children}.

Resolve the DOM root for server-driven F8: prefer div.project.root[projectid] (the currently zoomed Workflowy root), falling back to the first visible project row. Deliberately does NOT use resolveCurrentPreviewNode, because rooting at the hovered/focused #...--expand node makes Phase 2 discard that node as root and yields expand=0.

Top-level F8 keypress entry point (server-driven): resolve the currently-zoomed Workflowy root (resolveF8VisibleRootNode), serialize its visible DOM subtree tag-faithfully (serializeVisibleTreeForF8), await ensureSocketReady, request the server expansion plan (requestF8ExpansionPlan), and execute it (executeF8ExpansionPlan). Fail-loud, no client-side policy, no fallback.

Fire a render_markdown_modal WS request (client-minted request_id) and resolve with the server-composed Markdown result, or null on cold-socket/timeout so the caller can show the server-unavailable error in the dock. Supports DOM modal modes snapshot (all rows), rows_only (server-authored row list for captured tree), single (one focus_leaf row), and rows (frozen-DOM multi-select covering render with focus={mode:'rows'}).

THE success-paint primitive for the docked modal: renders a server-composed Markdown STRING into the bottom pane (truncation footer + Copy-MD source sync), sets dockedRenderedGoodUuid + dockedPaneHasGoodContent so a later transport failure preserves last-known-good, and returns true iff it painted non-empty. The single place 'good content is now on screen' is recorded; shared by the slice-snapshot, DOM-snapshot, DOM-single, and frozen code paths. Beaconed for the async-render-correctness slice (it is the paint half of the render-generation model + the intended success sink alongside renderDockedSelectionLocal).

Centralized capture of the `since` validation/empty-window signal from ANY docked-modal render reply (DOM or slice; snapshot, single, apply, refresh). On a since_error refusal (success:false + since_error) it stashes the human error string into dockedServerSinceError so applyDockedServerWarning paints the yellow bar at TOP priority (the render was refused -- supersedes the staleness/root bars); otherwise it clears the error and records empty_window (a VALID empty result -> an informational note, not an error). Also repaints the fine-print footer. Returns true iff a since_error was captured so callers can early-out (avoid the local-render fallback that would show stale content instead of teaching the invalid combination).

Phase 0 universal row adoption: whenever the server returned ordered rows (now EVERY snapshot, sorted or not), rebuild the docked top-half flat list from them -- the ONE server-authored occurrence-exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) row contract -- instead of the browser DOM walk; re-derives the browser-local per-row icon kind + hidden-children halo + el anchor from the live DOM keyed by uuid. Returns false only when there are NO server rows (cold socket), where the caller falls back to buildFlatVisibleNodeList. Supersedes the old sort-gated applySortedServerRows (kept as a thin alias).

FROZEN-DOM-SINGLE twin of applySortedServerRows (FIX 2 corollary). Rebuilds the docked top-half list from the server rows-only ordering of the captured frozen tree so a frozen sort's top list mirrors the bottom pane; carries the (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) triple for occurrence-exact per-row single renders. No-op (false) when unsorted / no rows.

Per-root-set/refresh: measure the visible tree and choose snapshot (pre-render all rows, cached) vs single (render-on-demand) vs local (cold-socket fallback); records cache_stale/root_matched for the warning bars. RENDER-GENERATION PARTICIPANT: bumps the shared monotonic dockedRenderGeneration on each prepare intent and gates its own snapshot install on it, so a superseded prepare cannot clobber a newer root's strategy. This is the DOM-render half of the ONE shared supersession clock the slice/push paint path also rides (see dockedRenderGeneration + displaySliceInDock). Tagged f8-expand so it surfaces in the async-render-correctness slice.

Renders the selected row's option-Y view across all sources (slice snapshot, slice single, frozen snapshot, DOM snapshot, DOM single). Captures the shared dockedRenderGeneration per async request (reqGeneration) and drops any reply whose generation is no longer current -- the DOM-render half of the ONE shared supersession clock the slice/push paint path also rides. Tagged f8-expand for the async-render-correctness slice.

THE transport-failure sink for the docked modal (misnamed 'local' -- there is NO local composition since the server became the sole renderer). Rule: if dockedPaneHasGoodContent it is a pure no-op (last-known-good is sacred -- suppresses spontaneous MV3/WebSocket-blip wipes); only on a genuine COLD START (pane never rendered) does it paint the actionable 'GLIMPSE server unavailable' message. This is the DOM-path error sink the G2 unified-error-sink work must fold together with the slice/push failure modes. Beaconed for the async-render-correctness slice.

Dock Refresh (ribbon ↻), the user's explicit re-sync gesture. Dispatches on render provenance: SLICE mode RE-APPLIES the same slice (requestSliceModalRender(dockedSliceContext.group_id) -> displaySliceInDock), re-projecting from the current nodes cache + group config + dock sort so edits made while curating a frozen slice are pulled in (deprecated nodes vanish, etc.); DOM mode re-walks the visible tree under dockedRootUuid and RESETS the bottom view to the root (index 0), deliberately NOT chasing the previously-selected row (occurrence can shift under sorting). Frozen-DOM rebuilds the in-memory snapshot and serves from it (no round trip).

Public entry for dock mode: ensures the panel, applies persisted width/split, and (re)roots the flat node list + rendered markdown at the focused Workflowy node; routed to from showMarkdownPreview when md_preview_docked is set
Capture-phase click/focusin listener that drives markdown preview popup visibility based on which Workflowy element the user is interacting with
Main standalone-client entrypoint: wait for DOM readiness, then initialize websocket connectivity plus UUID/F12/mutation helpers

python.comment: Local MCP-server request_id demultiplexer for the single server<->broker WebSocket. The BROKER already routes correlated replies to the correct MCP server process; this object performs the SECOND demux layer INSIDE that process: _ws_request_response registers request_id->Future before sending, and websocket_handler.put(...) resolves the exact Future instead of dropping frames through a shared FIFO. Non-correlated / unmatched frames still fall through to the legacy queue for existing consumers. This is what makes nested/concurrent Direction-A calls safe (server->tab command triggers tab->server handler triggers server->tab config read, etc.) without waiters cannibalizing each other's replies.

Module-level dict tracking in-memory asyncio jobs (ETCH, NEXUS, CARTO_BULK_APPLY). Populated by _start_background_job, scanned by mcp_job_status. RELEVANT TO F12+3 TIMEOUT INVESTIGATION: when 'MCP died' is observed, one diagnostic question is whether the foreground asyncio task representing _run_carto_bulk_visible_apply_job is still alive in this dict but stuck awaiting a downstream call — inspect via mcp_job_status. Detached CARTO_REFRESH workers do NOT live here; they're tracked via JSON files under cartographer_jobs/.
python.role: in-memory job registry for ETCH/NEXUS/CARTO async jobs

Reduces user-perceived dead-window from ~30s worst-case to ~0s.

python.comment: Path to the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip-toggle state file (wall-clock epoch deadline) in the runtime base dir. Shared by all MCP servers so the toggle is global under multi-server broker routing.
Read the shared skip-toggle wall-clock epoch deadline from disk (0.0 if absent/empty/unreadable). Best-effort; fail-open to 0.0 (toggle OFF).

Return True iff the user-controlled cache-refresh skip toggle is currently active. Reads the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline so the toggle is honored regardless of which MCP server (primary) does the work. Best-effort cleanup of the file once expired.
Seconds remaining on the skip toggle, or 0.0 if inactive/expired. Derived from the SHARED on-disk wall-clock deadline.
Enable/disable the shared cross-process cache-refresh skip toggle by writing/removing the wall-clock deadline file. Used by the set_cache_refresh_skip WebSocket handler.
Recover queued final responsibilities when a coordinator task ends before entering its worker; token-guarded receipts remain pending.
Coalesce reasons, fresh-fetch demand and fixed final obligations at one iteration cutoff; return scheduling/skip acknowledgment, never publication success.

Read-only heartbeat artifact merge for scanner/widget triage. Reports fresh/stale/missing/invalid identity and clamped mtime age without influencing persisted status, PID liveness, cancellation, reap, kill, admission, or claim repair.
One admission-mutex serialized inventory; public readable rows remain a list, internal observations retain uncertainty and incarnation provenance.
Admission-mutex cleanup of discharged orphan final-obligation records only; unfinished and retained-row receipts stay pinned for recovery/deduplication.

python.comment: Manual known-terminal history cleanup, additionally pinned by unfinished final-publication responsibility and live region claims. Only valid published/skipped exact-incarnation records permit removal; marker deletion uses the same admission mutex.

Persist latched relevance and positive terminal evidence; reconcile restart reservations via existing identity authority, never omission or age.
Serialize before off-loop scan through conservative durable observation and exact final-batch extraction; only positive stop proofs reserve work, execution receipts discharge it.

Exact token/incarnation final obligation transition under admission.mutex; unmatched callbacks release neither durable responsibility nor the live attempt; publication requires new-fetch receipt and adoption.

Watcher and startup trigger adapter for the single A1 governance sweep; supplies configured grace/cooldown values, loud diagnostics, and claim-aware terminal/orphan auxiliary cleanup without introducing a parallel lifecycle loop.

Derive a safe .md filename from a Workflowy node name for F12+4 materialize. Strips leading decoration/emoji, trailing #tags, illegal filename chars; collapses whitespace to underscores; guarantees a non-empty stem and a .md extension.

F12+4 leading-text fix: if the note's body (after optional YAML frontmatter) starts with prose BEFORE the first Markdown heading, synthesize a leading '# Leading text' H1 above that prose so the pre-heading text is not lost when the note is split into a heading subtree. No-op when the body already opens with a heading or is empty.

F12+4 hygiene: strip a LEADING Cartographer metadata block (MD_PATH: … --- or BEACON (…) … ---) from a node's note before materializing it to a .md. Needed because a Dump-Bay child that was already written back to the primary file via F12+3 carries such a block at the top of its note; without stripping it, that metadata would be written into the new .md as body content (and then split into bogus child nodes). Mirrors markdown_roundtrip._strip_md_path_block / _strip_md_ast_beacon_block but kept local to avoid importing module privates.

Bulk F12+4 helper: classify a node's note as a Cartographer FILE/FOLDER header. Returns ('Root'|'Path', value) or None using the strict first-line-only _extract_path_header_from_note. A folder/path node has a header whose value has no recognized file extension; a file node's value has one (e.g. .md/.py).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a Markdown file (.md/.markdown)? Used by the bulk walk + eligibility classifier to decide whether to recurse INTO a file node (markdown -> yes; any other extension -> skip+prune).

Bulk F12+4 helper: does a Cartographer Path: value name a FILE (has a filename extension) rather than a FOLDER segment? A folder node's Path: is a bare segment (no dot-extension); a file node's Path: ends in an extension. Used to distinguish path/folder nodes (recurse through) from file nodes (skip unless .md). Thin wrapper: the canonical implementation now lives in api_client_nexus (single source of truth, co-located with _extract_path_header_from_note + _classify_node_map_state); imported here via a function-scoped local import to avoid the api_client_nexus->server cycle, mirroring the other unguarded server->client local imports. NO inline fallback copy on purpose: a bool predicate has no safe 'unknown' value (returning False would mislabel a real file node as a folder and misroute the F12 menus), and if api_client_nexus is unimportable the whole server is non-functional anyway -- so we let the import raise loudly rather than keep a divergent second copy of the logic.

FIRST server-queried F12 menu-visibility check. Walks UP the nodes-export cache ancestor chain (zoom-proof, unlike the DOM) to classify the hovered node, then combines that with the client-reported visible/hidden child booleans to decide whether the F12+4 entry appears and which bulk sub-options enable. Returns {show, mode, visible_option_enabled, all_option_enabled, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+4 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_materialize). Reads node_id + has_visible_children/has_hidden_children from the payload, runs _classify_bulk_materialize_eligibility, and echoes the verdict back (with node_id for client-side correlation).

Zoom-proof resolver for F12+3: given ANY node_id, walk UP the /nodes-export cache ancestor chain (which never hides anything, unlike the zoomed-in DOM) to find the enclosing Markdown FILE node. If the node itself IS a markdown FILE node, returns it. Crucially IGNORES the md-in-md temp node's SECOND-line Path: (that node is never a reverse-Markdown target); the true primary file is the enclosing markdown FILE ancestor. Returns the FILE node's UUID, or None when no enclosing markdown file exists (e.g. inside a non-markdown file, or no file at all).

Cache-backed (zoom-proof) eligibility classifier for the BULK F12+3 menu entry. Decision tree is SIMPLER than F12+4 (no submenu for availability, no child-visibility input needed to decide SHOW): a markdown FILE node -> single F12+3 (mode='single', no bulk entry); a node INSIDE a mapped file -> no bulk entry (degenerates to standard single F12+3 on the enclosing file, which the server resolves zoom-safely); any node that is NOT a file node and NOT inside a file (a folder/Root: node OR a plain unmapped Workflowy node) -> bulk. Returns {show, mode, reason, classification}.

WebSocket handler for the bulk-F12+3 eligibility query (action=classify_bulk_f12p3). Reads node_id, runs _classify_bulk_f12p3_eligibility, echoes the verdict {show,mode,reason,classification} back (with node_id for client-side correlation). No child-visibility input is needed (F12+3 bulk has no availability submenu).

Bulk F12+3 collection walk (source-agnostic, mirrors _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves plumbing). DFS over a tree (client visible-DOM payload OR nodes-export cache subtree) gathering MARKDOWN FILE nodes only. Per-node rules: a markdown FILE node QUALIFIES and we do NOT descend into it (F12+3 regenerates the whole file from its Workflowy subtree); a non-markdown FILE node is skipped+pruned; folder/Root: nodes and plain nodes are recursed THROUGH. Uses the universal first-line-only header classifier, so a md-in-md temp node (Path on line 2) is never mistaken for a file node. Returns ordered list of {id,name} file-node descriptors.

Bulk F12+3 execution handler (action=bulk_generate_markdown). Echoes request_id. Never forces a /nodes-export refresh (detect+warn staleness). Deterministic + pure -- the same row produces the same key on the original render and on any re-projection (MATCH = EMIT).

Build the SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE render_scope echo object for a cache-projected render. This is the ONE object every consumer (client adoptRenderScope -> per-tab render state + ribbon widgets + footer; and the MCP push tool output) treats as the normalized ground truth of what was ACTUALLY rendered, regardless of which SURFACE (ribbon click or MCP glimpse() call) triggered the render. Carries ONLY the normalized structured render-defining fields: scope identity (kind/group_id/group_name/root_uuid) + view params (sort_by/sort_direction/since object-or-null/headings_only). There is no pre-composed display string -- the status footer is the ONE consumer that renders a human string, composing it from THESE fields, so string-composition lives in exactly one place. kind is 'slice' (group at its own root), 'slice_override' (group tags scoped to an override root), 'raw_root' (bare root_uuid raw dump, no group -> the footer labels it 'raw dump of <root8>'), or 'lightning_rod' (a temporary Lightning Rod selection via the `lightning` param, which takes PRECEDENCE). LIGHTNING SELECTION: a lightning render carries ONE opaque `selection` object {mode:'gather'|'render_tags'|'render_search'|'render_symbols', + per-mode fields (tags+postfix_policy | query/query_mode | symbols/root_uuids/favor) + match_scope} that the client round-trips VERBATIM for BEHAVIOR (routing is by selection.mode, never selection_kind). selection_kind ('gather'|'tags'|'search'|'symbols') + workflowy_search_equivalent are DERIVED from selection.mode and are DISPLAY-ONLY (footer/status-bar label). UNMOORED SIGNAL: live_gui_sync_supported is a TOP-LEVEL bool emitted for EVERY kind (+ live_gui_sync_skipped_reason naming why when False) -- False for a raw dump (no membership search), a descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' render (inexpressible as a Workflowy search), a search_too_many_variants refusal, or any lightning selection; the client surfaces the unmoored state on the yellow bar. It is DISPLAY/observability only, never a behavior driver. EVERY kind also carries the explicit CONTENT/TREE CONTRACT fields content_format ('markdown'|'raw_text') + tree_mode ('render_tree'|'root_only') so the client never guesses how to paint the one rendered string or populate the top-half list (only a lightning GATHER is raw_text/root_only today). Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

python.comment: Phase-E1 SPEC-AWARE BRIDGE to the ONE render_scope composer. Given a RESOLVED RenderProjectionSpec (kind/root/group already canonicalized by the caller's resolution step -- NOT the raw incoming spec), DELEGATE to _compose_render_scope by unpacking exactly the scalar params it already takes (Option A, Dan-decided: delegate, do NOT reimplement from spec.to_render_scope_fields(), so there stays ONE render_scope-assembly implementation and this never becomes a second scope factory / caller-side fabrication site). The is_raw_dump / root_overridden booleans the scalar composer wants are read straight off the spec's kind-derived properties (spec.is_raw_dump / spec.root_overridden), and sort_by is passed via spec.sort_by_internal() (the ONE wire-'none'<->internal-None translation). search_too_many_variants is a POST-RENDER fact (not a spec input field, per invariant 5) so it is threaded as an explicit kwarg here, exactly as the scalar composer already accepts it. This is the E1 seam that lets every downstream server call site (modal handler E3, content-return GLIMPSE paths E4, push frame E5) compose render_scope FROM the same spec it projected from, instead of from a parallel bag of locals -- the two-parallel-assembly-points seam Phase E removes. Pure + deterministic; no I/O.

The ONE inherited slice-group root policy seam shared by MCP/lens renders and every stored-root consumer (APPLY, copy-search, named merge, scoped reprojection, push and group purge). Delegates resolution to resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle with the caller's pinned map; exact UUIDs, clean prefixes including 8 hex, and AP-IDs are adopted with existing archive semantics. Corrective UUID shaves are rejected and only their speculative correction echo is discarded. Transport, scope notes and miss envelopes stay per-origin; explicit input roots keep the standard forgiving boundary.

PURE formatter for the ambiguous/missing error ENVELOPE returned by the cache-projection root_uuid resolution sites (the bare-root RAW-DUMP GLIMPSE, the slice-group override root, the push scope root, and Lightning Rod). Given a resolve_uuid_like_node_handle result that did NOT resolve (candidates present => ambiguous; else => missing), returns the standard {success:False, error, [candidates/matched_prefix_len/truncated], **extra} dict -- so the several sites can't DRIFT on the field set. Deliberately NOT a resolver wrapper: each caller keeps its own resolution and control flow (plain return vs await _reply) and its own error WORDING (via display/label); this only unifies the payload SHAPE. Chain-1 W4 (F5): in the MISSING branch, a refusal-reason operation (a sink, a write, an export, a purge preview) whose root names a visible archived node RAISES ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError with the exact §5.2/§5.3 text and provenance — before any file/modal/preview work; reads (reason None/flag) and no-context callers keep today's hint-only text. Returns None when the handle actually resolved (caller should not call it then). Pure; no I/O.

ONE handler for every cache-projected docked-modal render + per-row re-render (the 'Apply slice' feature). Resolves the four-cell scope truth table: slice (group_id), slice_override (group_id+root_uuid), raw_root (root_uuid only), lightning_rod (lightning{mode,...}; group-less, Phase-1-only via an injected member_predicate BY DEFAULT -- render_tags + postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) upgrades the cell to the shared build_stage1_base_tree funnel with one nested postfix config read). Lightning modes: gather (short-circuits to the raw-text tag outline), render_tags{tags} (DEFAULT: no config read; 'slice': one nested postfix config read), render_search{query,query_mode} (both scope via one frame root_uuid), and render_symbols{symbols,root_uuids,favor} (the tag-free beacon slice: roots via its own root_uuids -> their LCA, does one nested config read for the global-suppression filter, resolves via the shared _project_render_symbols_from_cache, and appends its unresolved/ambiguous report to the full-document reply), plus render_lens{lens,query?} (the recursive LensSpec cell: one nested config read, the shared immutable Stage-0 snapshot + transport-free _project_render_lens_from_cache, derived-LCA rooting, and explicit empty artifact). All five modes emit one opaque `selection` object into the render_scope. Then runs the shared projection -> prepare_stage2_render_forest -> rows -> snapshot-vs-single machinery and echoes the server-authoritative render_scope.

Bulk F12+4 qualification walk (source-agnostic). DFS over a tree (fed EITHER by the client visible-DOM payload OR the nodes-export cache subtree) applying the rules: recurse THROUGH folder/path nodes; into .md file nodes; SKIP+prune non-md file nodes; never qualify a node with children; qualify a childless non-path/non-file node iff its note (leading metadata block stripped) parses to >=1 markdown heading via _note_body_has_heading. Returns the ordered list of qualifying leaf descriptors.

Bulk F12+4 (mode B, recurse-all-incl-hidden) tree source: build a nested {id,name,note,children[]} subtree rooted at root_uuid directly from the /nodes-export cache, ignoring Workflowy expansion state entirely (like F12+3's synthetic-tree path). Returns the root node dict, or None if root not in cache.

Bulk F12+4 filename assignment. ONE accumulating pass over the full qualifying-leaf set: derive each leaf's stem (FILEBASE-ancestor prefix + sanitized node name, same logic as single-node F12+4) and resolve collisions against BOTH on-disk files AND already-assigned in-set names (siblings can share identical markdown headings). The in-set reservation makes prior leaves act as though already on disk so the integer-suffix increment is race-free and deterministic.

Bulk F12+4 execution handler (action=bulk_materialize_markdown). Builds the tree (mode='visible' -> client visible_tree payload; mode='all' -> cache subtree), runs _collect_bulk_materialize_leaves, assigns collision-safe filenames across the whole in-memory set FIRST (single accumulating process, race-free), then for EACH qualifying leaf writes the metadata-stripped note to its .md, sets the node note (Path: header for persist, dummy MD_PATH: block for in-md-file persist, or clears for temp), patches the snapshot, and fires an INDEPENDENT detached F12+1 job per leaf (N status lines, no parent coordinator -- per Dan).

Browser-initiated UUID Explorer anchor-list convenience endpoint. Client formats it as UUID/name text and copies/displays it; no client-side anchor enumeration logic.

The ONE module-level coroutine the WS reader loop spawns (via create_isolated_context_task) for the long handlers whose inline failure frame was the generic {action, success:false, node_id, error} shape, instead of awaiting the handler inline: the two F12 refresh actions and (since U4) open_node_in_windsurf / materialize_markdown_file / bulk_materialize_markdown / bulk_generate_markdown. WebSocket handler for the widget's once-a-second CARTO jobs poll (action=carto_list_jobs), spawned by the pump through _carto_list_jobs_poll (single-flight + 0.5 s spacing: the reply is untargeted, so the broker broadcasts it to every tab and a coalesced poll loses nothing). Cache-free (tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json); same carto_list_jobs_result wire shapes and error log line as before

WebSocket handler for the widget's 'Clear job history' sweep (action=carto_clear_job_history). Cache-free by classification (tests/coherence_s03b_registry.json ws_actions.cache_free -- cancellation sentinel only), so it carries NO @_ws_cache_boundary, exactly like the inline clause it replaced. Delegates to the SAME _system_job_cancel_impl the system.job.cancel MCP verb uses; owns its shaped carto_cancel_job_result frames (unchanged wire shape)

python.comment: Diagnostic-only residue behind node.edit note search-and-replace. Runs ONLY after exact and 1:1 Unicode-space-fold matching both miss. First probes a space-folded + zero-width-stripped view with an original-index map (never silently mutates through this non-1:1 tier); then a conservative unique visible-token anchor. When a probable region exists, returns the note's ACTUAL substring as suggested_search plus a ready-to-reissue {search,replace} suggested_edit and the first divergent Unicode codepoints. The edit report JSON is ensure_ascii=True, making invisible characters visible/copyable as \\uXXXX. Pure; no I/O.

ONE per-entry note search authority for node.edit single/multi modes. First match by default; replace_all chooses all non-overlapping matches from the pre-entry text without reprocessing replacements. Exact matches anywhere win globally; only an exact miss permits 1:1 Unicode SPACE SEPARATOR folding. Folded matches reuse the original source-context-preserving splicer so unchanged NBSP indentation survives. Returns first index and optional tier/near_miss; replace-all adds a replacement_count. Pure text transformation, no I/O or cache mutation.

THE one note-diff renderer behind every note-edit report (search/replace and whole-note — the public default since [ap:4JSBO5]). Stdlib difflib only; line-oriented. Size-guarded by the ONE shared head+tail clamp (snippet_view.clamp_span_to_head_tail — the same arithmetic the read guard uses) at DEFAULT_NOTE_MAX_LINES: past the threshold the middle is elided behind ONE row naming the omitted diff-line region, the hidden hunk count and the whole-diff totals (+added / -removed); an EMPTY before-note renders the one line 'note was empty; N lines written' instead of a wall of + lines. Pure; no I/O; no second clamp and no second diff renderer exist.

Public edit surface (legacy workflowy_edit_node + consolidated node.edit). Thin wrapper over _node_edit_core with NO internal channels: every name edit runs the protected-name policy (_compose_protected_name) -- supplied trailing #tags or an added/changed leading [ap:] handle are loud ProtectedNameViolations; existing tags/AP-ID auto-preserve. [ap:4JSBO5]: the whole-note diff default is resolved HERE (return_diff tri-state: omitted + note -> true) so internal narrow channels never build diffs, and the public plain-update ack is converted HERE from the core's redacted WorkFlowyNode into the [ap:PHO4BG] small dict -- node fields minus note/children (and the model_dump mirrors no/ch), plus note_written/note_chars/note_lines when a note was written; never a "note": null.

python.comment: Shared async core behind workflowy_edit_node / node.edit AND the narrow internal protected-region channels. Every name write is composed from ONE live GET snapshot (memoized _fetch_current_node; note search/replace and opt-in whole-note return_diff reuse the SAME node, so a name+note combo costs one read + one write) via the pure _compose_protected_name policy -- supplied trailing #tags or a new/changed leading [ap:] handle raise ProtectedNameViolation (loud, zero mutation); existing tags/AP-ID auto-preserve, and a rename also preserves the ordinary title's leading emoji run (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F: you need not pass an emoji; a supplied run wins explicitly; _replace_leading_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied title wholesale). Internal callers get exactly ONE narrow channel, never a generic infrastructure bypass: anchor.dock.update passes _tag_transform; anchor.point.assign_id passes _assign_ap_core; anchor.point.remove_id passes _remove_ap_id; the node emoji verbs (update_emoji / prepend_emoji / append_emoji) pass _leading_emoji_mutation; anchor.point.touch passes _touch (a content-preserving modifiedAt advance: echo the live layoutMode with zero text bytes on the wire, or fall back to an identity name recomposition when no echoable layoutMode exists; never composes text itself; returns the UNREDACTED post-write node so the caller can verify preservation); all may inject _current_node to reuse their own live read.

THE ONE substantive implementation behind the three node leading-emoji verbs (update_emoji replace/remove, prepend_emoji before the run, append_emoji after the run). Resolves the node handle, performs one authoritative live read, composes the request through _compose_protected_name's typed narrow LeadingEmojiMutation channel, returns a true zero-write no-op when unchanged (reachable in practice only from update_emoji -- the insert verbs always change the name), and otherwise injects the SAME snapshot into _node_edit_core for one write. Only the leading emoji run of the ordinary name section is affected; AP-ID, legacy decoration before AP, ordinary title, middle/right emojis, trailing tags, and descendants are preserved. The three thin verb delegates below stay beaconless on purpose (curate, don't carpet-bomb) -- they remain Cartographer AST-mapped and symbol-resolvable under this parent.

THE ONE substantive implementation behind the two node note-concat verbs (append_note / prepend_note, [ap:MZOKZ1]): an agent whose note is too big for one tool call writes it in parts -- point.capture the first part, then append/prepend the rest one part per call, no sentinel and no search string. Resolves the mutator handle, performs ONE authoritative live read + wire-to-semantic decode through _read_live_node_note (newline-normalized to pure LF exactly as the note search-and-replace path does), concatenates the non-empty text with the EXPLICIT separator (default '\n'; skipped when the existing note is empty -- there is nothing to separate), and writes once through _node_edit_core(note=..., _current_node=<the same live node>) so the whole verb is one read + one governed write. Byte-exact on the semantic domain; no diff (the point is size); AP-ID, title and trailing tags are untouched (a note-only request composes no name). Empty text is a loud ValueError, never a silent no-op. No mapped-node refusal: parity with node.edit, which refuses none (checked at e5a86ce). The two thin verb delegates below stay one-line re-fronts (curate, don't carpet-bomb).
Thin re-front for node.append_note over the ONE _node_note_concat_impl (position='append'): the text lands AFTER the existing note, joined by the explicit separator (default newline).
Thin re-front for node.prepend_note over the ONE _node_note_concat_impl (position='prepend'): the text lands BEFORE the existing note, joined by the explicit separator (default newline).

python.comment: Shared handle-resolution front door for the MUTATOR tools (workflowy_edit_node / delete_node / complete_node / uncomplete_node / move_node). Mirrors _resolve_tag_node_id but for mutators: routes the supplied handle through the Layer-3 universal resolver client.resolve_node_handle(prefer='uuid', allow_uuid=True, allow_symbol=True) so a mutator gains the SAME UUID-hallucination grace the tag tools got in Commit 1 (exact hit -> unique prefix -> ambiguous STOP -> symbol fallback) instead of posting a raw node_id to a zero-tolerance REST endpoint. UUID leg self-loads the cache (resolve-only; no map reuse downstream). DIFFERENCE from the tag path: a mutator that cannot identify its target must FAIL LOUDLY, not silently no-op -- so on ambiguous/unresolved this RAISES RuntimeError with actionable guidance (candidates listed on ambiguity) rather than returning a friendly no-op dict. On success returns the single resolved UUID. label is the tool name, used only in messages. The RAW REST client methods (WorkFlowyClientCore.update_node/move_node/...) stay exact-UUID-only by design: resolution belongs at the BOUNDARY (here), not in transport.
python.role: resolve a mutator tool's node handle via the universal resolver (prefer=uuid, symbol allowed)

python.comment: Shared boundary front door for the NON-mutating, NON-symbol GENERIC-NODE tools (workflowy_read_node / workflowy_export_node / raw workflowy_etch parent_id / create_anchor parent_uuid). The NARROW sibling of _resolve_mutator_node_id: it routes the handle through resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle (UUID exact -> UUID unique-prefix -> [ap:CORE] AP-ID; ambiguous STOPS, only fully-unresolved falls through), deliberately WITHOUT the source-code SYMBOL domain -- a function name resolving to some mapped node is a footgun when the slot names a plain Workflowy node to read/export/parent. Self-loads the /nodes-export cache (resolve-only; cache-only, no rate-limited refresh). python.comment: GLIMPSE `since` Form-A window PARSER. Parses a time-window token into a duration in SECONDS (timestamps are epoch-seconds). Accepts a unit-suffixed integer/float -- s(econds) m(inutes) h(ours) d(ays) w(eeks) -- e.g. '3d','1w','12h','90m','45s'; a BARE number is interpreted as DAYS ('7' == '7d'), the common case. Whitespace-tolerant, case-insensitive. Returns None for a blank/None/garbage/non-positive token so the caller can raise an actionable error. Pure. | GLIMPSE `since` PRUNE -- the shared leaf-branch filter run LAST (after Phase1/2/3 AND after the timestamp reorder), on the already-final sorted forest. Decomposes the forest into root->leaf branches (same DFS the sort uses), keeps a branch iff its branch-date (via the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static -- created=leaf createdAt, modified=branch-max modifiedAt, IDENTICAL to the sort) is beyond the pivot: ascending -> STRICTLY GREATER than pivot (most-recent tail; the pivot node itself excluded, everything newer kept); descending -> STRICTLY LESS than pivot (the commensurate 'oldest tail', a don't-care corner but done right). A branch with no resolvable date is DROPPED (can't prove it's in the window). Then trie-merges the surviving branches back into a tree via the SAME _reorder pass with sort_by carried through, so straddled ancestors re-emit exactly as in the unfiltered render. Returns a NEW forest (inputs untouched); empty list when nothing survives.

GLIMPSE `since` Form-A (time-window) PIVOT. Data-relative leading edge (Dan): the pivot is the branch-date of the MOST RECENT leaf branch in the ALREADY-FINAL forest (ascending) minus the window -- so 'last 1 week' on data whose newest branch is 2 years old means the week ENDING at that 2-year-old edge, NOT wall-clock now. Descending flips to the OLDEST edge plus the window (the don't-care commensurate corner). Uses the SHARED _branch_timestamp_key_static for every branch date so it matches the sort. Returns the pivot epoch-seconds, or None if no branch has a resolvable date (caller then returns the tree unfiltered rather than erroring on empty data).

GLIMPSE `since="curated"` FORM-B PIVOT (the self-maintaining curation cursor). Walks the /nodes-export cache subtree under root_uuid, finds every node that has been CURATED = carries any tag matching an active slice prefix INCLUDING --deprecated variants but EXCLUDING the --suppress/--expand PRESENTATION variants (via node_is_curated_for_prefixes, threaded with the render caller's resolved match_scope -- the SAME SELECTION-stage scope knob Stage-1 membership uses, 'name' = title only so a note-body family tag never moves the cursor, 'name_and_note' = default NAME+NOTE -- deliberately looser than slice MEMBERSHIP on the triage axis, because deprecating a tag is itself a curation act the user must not re-encounter; suppressing/expanding one is a lens carve-out, NOT triage, and must not move the cursor -- Session-019 curated-cursor fix + match_scope plumbing). For each curated node it computes that node's branch-date using the SAME rule the sort uses (_branch_timestamp_key_static over the node's root->leaf cache path: created=the curated node's own createdAt; modified=branch-max modifiedAt down to it), and returns the MAX (ascending; MIN for descending) = the high-water mark. Everything strictly newer than this in the shared-tail prune is the UNCURATED tail. Returns None when NOTHING under root is curated yet (no group tag anywhere) so the tail shows the whole subtree (all of it is 'new since last curated'). Cache-only; pure aside from the cache read.
Count every node in a nested {children:[...]} subtree, inclusive of the root.
Maximum depth of a nested {children:[...]} subtree (a childless root is depth 1).

The shared STAGE-2 final-forest preparation: timestamp sort -> since prune -> empty-window detection -> node_count/depth, over a STAGE-1 base tree. Three render sites call it -- render_stage2_filter_sort (the GLIMPSE tail), _handle_render_slice_modal (the Apply-slice modal), and _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture (the frozen-DOM render_spec=modal sibling) -- so all three produce an identical final forest. Returns the final forest as a tree OBJECT (not just a rendered string) because the modal walks it to build its rows / per-row views / last-N label. PURE: no WebSocket, no config read. It does NOT compute the curated pivot -- the caller passes curated_pivot_ts in, because that pivot needs the slice's active_prefixes. recent_by ([ap:TVIIBN] 4d(a)) is the recency basis of a 'newest' item_count selection, threaded verbatim into apply_since_to_forest (None = resolve at apply: the sort axis when it is a timestamp, else modified -- the ONE resolve_item_count_basis rule). Returns (forest, since_applied, empty_window, node_count, depth, since_err); since_err is surfaced (never swallowed) so each caller shapes its own error reply.

python.comment: STAGE 2 (filter+sort+render): the shared render/sort/write tail for every cache-sourced GLIMPSE (slice-group, bare root_uuid, and Lightning Rod). Runs OVER an already-built STAGE-1 base tree and does PRESENTATION only -- it never re-decides membership. Delegates the sort/since/empty-window/count prep to prepare_stage2_render_forest, then renders through the same composer the live-DOM GLIMPSE uses (_build_markdown_preview_from_tree in markdown mode, _annotate_preview_ids_and_build_tree in full/UUID mode), optionally resolving a row focus to render one node's option-Y view. headings_only renders also carry dock.peek's four-field end-of-line vocabulary ([ap:UH0UOU]): the source_metrics index is built once here (build_render_source_metrics over this render's top-level root) and rides the policy; managed source lines (Cartographer/beacon markers) stay bare. Optionally writes a single compact .md (full-mode disk export is caller-guarded, not here). Merges the caller's source_meta into the payload. NODE LIMIT ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2): the optional max_nodes/member_predicate pair -- passed ONLY by the search surfaces (slice_group.sift / lightning_rod.render_search headings tiers) -- caps the final forest to the first N MATCHING nodes AFTER the sort and the since prune via cap_forest_to_first_node_count, recomputes node_count/depth over what actually renders, and echoes node_limit_applied (the shaper's node-limit line composes from it); every other caller passes neither and stays byte-identical. LENS SCAFFOLD ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g): the optional lens_scaffold_ids set -- passed ONLY by the lens render tails (the caller folds the ancestor_notes opt-out) -- forwards the lens's connective scaffolding above the input roots to BOTH materialize calls' lens-scaffold-ancestor cause, so that ancestor path renders headings-only in Markdown AND full/UUID mode, document order included; every other caller passes nothing and stays byte-identical. Knows NOTHING about slice-group or root_uuid resolution. REPOSITORY VIEW (U1): with spec.repository_view the projection (_repository_view_forest) runs after the prepare/cap steps (a multi-root render refuses), the projected forest materializes with document order / no focus / no chronological suppression, D = composed + one final newline, the payload and the output_file ack carry the repository_view counts (+ document on the in-memory payload), and the file write delivers D exactly -- never the coherence advisory (§6.3).

python.comment: render_symbols PER-ITEM OBJECT ELEMENTS (ap:EXPSWP; D2 input shape Option B; D3 unwrap-only in v1): the ONE shared item normalizer for the render_symbols `symbols` list. An element is either a plain string handle (today's behavior, stripped) or a small object {'uuid': HANDLE | 'symbol': NAME, 'expand'?: bool} -- exactly one of uuid/symbol, non-empty string handle, expand bool if present (absent/false = plain member). Returns {ok, handles (resolution input, strings only), expand_handles (flagged handles, expand-wins on a plain+flagged duplicate per the locked semantics contract), raw (the canonical VERBATIM echo list: stripped strings + shallow-copied objects -- what the spec / wire blob / render_scope selection carries so every re-projection re-runs normalize->resolve->sweep deterministically, D5)}. LOUD structured rejection (success:False-shaped): both keys, neither key, empty/non-string handle, non-bool expand, unrecognized keys, or any element that is neither string nor dict. The uuid/symbol KEY is NOT honored as an explicit-kind resolution hint in v1 (unwrap-only; the handle flows through the existing favor classification) -- a v1.1 nicety. Used by ALL THREE entry surfaces (_lightning_rod_render_symbols, the _handle_render_slice_modal render_symbols branch, and the _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal render_symbols branch), replacing the three hand-rolled [str(s).strip() ...] coercions (a net de-duplication).

DYNAMIC TAG-FREE BEACON SLICE (Lightning Rod mode='render_symbols'). Resolves a mixed list of UUIDs and/or symbols (function/class/beacon names) per-item, UUID-first then symbol-fallback (favor flag), scopes to REQUIRED root_uuids (single or list), applies ABSOLUTE global-suppression filtering (option B) then buckets survivors resolved(1)/ambiguous(N)/unresolved(0)/out-of-scope.
