Chain-2 r2 (R1): a SHAVED corrective match of the stored root is REJECTED, never adopted — the stored identity and the pre-r1 miss policy are preserved (uuid_resolution_was_shave classifies the outcome; the speculative correction echo is surgically discarded; the raw root falls to the absent-root branch) — while an exact archived record still beats a shave upstream (E2) and keeps the archive repair. No second resolver and no per-carrier banner copy: the lens group atom's inherited root shares this exact seam via lens_engine._resolve_root.
yaml.role: async _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache(slice_group, as_markdown, output_file, sort_by, sort_direction, target_tab)

yaml.comment: PUSH-TO-MODAL path for glimpse(push_to_modal=True): instead of RETURNING the rendered content to the agent, it COMMANDS the target Workflowy tab to render the requested SERVER-SIDE SCOPE into its docked Markdown modal -- the server-push twin of a human clicking APPLY. Chain-1 W4 (F5): the funnel's resolve-HERE-before-the-round-trip doctrine now covers the render_lens cell's atom roots too -- a root naming a visible archived node raises the §5.3.2 archived_node_read_only refusal (the docked modal never serves archives), so a push can never ack success and then fail tab-side. Chain-1 r2 (R2-W2): the resolve-HERE doctrine now covers every indirect selection as well -- a render_lens GROUP atom pre-flights its group's STORED root (an explicit root_handle override is the target and wins; a bare group atom rides the stored default, so a recursive merged lens cannot hide an archived effective root), the render_symbols cell resolves its roots and runs its items through the SHARED _resolve_lightning_rod_symbol_items_from_cache router (live legs first; an archived root or item refuses before any command; items still ride verbatim per D5), and the direct slice-group cell resolves the chosen group's STORED root when no override root is present. Handles the full (slice_group, root_uuid) truth table: slice_group only (resolve id-or-name -> canonical group_id via the SHARED Layer-1 _resolve_slice_group_handle -- the SAME id/prefix/case-insensitive-name resolver _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache uses), root_uuid only (resolve prefix-tolerantly via the SHARED resolve_uuid_like_node_handle -> a RAW-DUMP push, the zero-token 'show me this anchor' command), or BOTH (slice lens scoped to an override root). All resolution happens HERE (before the round-trip) so a bad group name / missing UUID fails loudly early. Sends a Direction-A 'apply_slice_in_dock' frame carrying whichever of {group_id, root_uuid} are present + the AGENT-SUPPLIED sort/since as an EXPLICIT override (never the tab's global dock sort) via the generic _ws_request_response rail; returns the tab's ack. The tab-side dispatch invokes the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock (same fn the APPLY button uses), so the dock render + (for a slice) live-GUI-sync watcher are identical to a manual Apply; a raw-dump push installs NO watcher (no search/plan). The caller (glimpse) guards a bare live-DOM push (neither scope) as the only error.

UUID-hallucination HARDENING for a render_spec-driven GLIMPSE (the render_spec="modal"/blob path). Given a deserialized RenderProjectionSpec + the /nodes-export cache map, canonicalize EVERY UUID the spec carries -- root_uuid, focus.uuid, and EVERY focus.ancestor_path entry -- through the SHARED prefix-tolerant Layer-1 resolver resolve_uuid_like_node_handle (the exact machine SCRY / anchor / snippet callers use). Grace runs BEFORE the exact (uuid, ancestor_path, occurrence) focus match downstream, so it only CANONICALIZES a possibly-drifted string to its cache UUID; it NEVER loosens the occurrence-exact match itself (a canonicalized triple still resolves to exactly one occurrence via _resolve_focus_index_path). On the render_spec="modal" path the UUIDs are already server-canonical (near-no-op belt-and-suspenders); on the pasted-blob fallback path this is the real net against an agent-drifted UUID in the chain. A UUID that stays unresolved (no exact hit, no unique prefix) or is ambiguous is LEFT AS-IS (best-effort): a bad focus already fails safe to the whole document downstream, and a bad root_uuid surfaces its own cache-miss error in the dispatch that follows. Returns a NEW spec via with_overrides; the input spec (frozen) is never mutated. Pure; no I/O beyond reading the passed cache map.

Dispatch a resolved RenderProjectionSpec to the right cache-render helper by spec.kind -- the shared tail for BOTH render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (the "modal" WS query and the pasted-blob fallback). It routes the (slice|slice_override) cells to _glimpse_slice_group_from_cache (passing spec.group_id as slice_group, the resolved root as root_uuid_override for slice_override, and spec.focus) and the raw_root cell to _glimpse_root_uuid_from_cache (passing spec.root_uuid + spec.focus). The lightning_rod cell (ap:GLMPMODAL) re-projects the FOURTH scope by reading spec.lightning['mode'] and calling the SAME projector a fresh lightning_rod() call uses (_lightning_rod_from_cache for gather/render_tags/render_search; _lightning_rod_render_symbols for render_symbols): the opaque lightning selection is passed through verbatim, so no new render path is introduced. Each mode keeps its own constraints (render_symbols Markdown-only + roots via its own selection.root_uuids; gather raw-text/root_only; since='curated' rejected inside the projector). FOCUS on a lightning modal read is now SUPPORTED for the node-tree modes (render_tags/render_search/render_symbols): spec.focus is threaded into the projector and resolved occurrence-exactly by the shared render_stage2_filter_sort focus authority -- the ONLY residual rejection is gather+focus (a gather is a tag outline with one synthetic root row, so a real row focus is a category error). Every view knob (as_markdown / sort / since / headings_only / match_scope / descend_policy) is read off the spec, so the render is byte-identical to the equivalent explicit-arg GLIMPSE -- the whole point of routing through the ONE spec object. descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' is honored for the raw_root cell by building the anchor-boundary predicate here (the one config-read WS touch), exactly as the explicit-arg root_uuid path does.

The AGENT-OVERRIDE seam for the render_spec-driven GLIMPSE paths (render_spec="modal" AND the pasted-blob fallback). Given the RESOLVED, tab-sourced (or pasted) RenderProjectionSpec and the agent's TRI-STATE view overrides (as_markdown / headings_only / sort_by / sort_direction / since; None = inherit what the modal is showing, a value = explicit override), it (1) merges the non-None overrides onto the spec via the SINGLE normalized mutator spec.with_view_overrides (which re-runs the ONE normalizer and preserves the resolved kind via kind_hint -- NOT raw with_overrides), then (2) runs the LOUD combination guards ONCE on the FINAL merged spec, where spec.focus and spec.kind are known. The two guards (Dan-decided): (A) a sort override (sort_by/sort_direction supplied) is REJECTED when spec.focus is present -- sorting a single focused option-Y row is ill-defined; the user re-roots the modal at that subtree instead; (B) a since override is REJECTED when spec.focus is present (a tail/window over the whole underlying scope intersected with a focused row is meaningless). Beyond focus, the standard since preconditions are enforced by reading the FINAL SinceSpec object fields; curated requires a slice/slice_override scope. Returns (spec, None) on success or (spec, error_dict) on a rejected combination. This is the ONLY place agent view overrides are applied to a render_spec spec, so both render_spec sub-paths share ONE override+guard implementation.

Pure pre-order DFS that returns the FIRST node in a forest whose id/uuid matches -- the CANONICAL (unsorted) node lookup for the Scoped Lightning Rod occurrence-exact re-root pre-step in _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture. After the sorted forest is pruned to a clicked occurrence and that occurrence's LEAF UUIDs are collected, this locates the clicked node's canonical node in the UNSORTED captured forest so its subtree can be rebuilt DE-MIRRORED (filtered to those leaf UUIDs via build_selected_subtree_from_forest). Relies on the v1 invariant that a Workflowy UUID appears AT MOST ONCE in the raw (unsorted) tree -- Workflowy 'mirrors' are explicitly UNSUPPORTED in v1 -- so 'the first match' IS 'the only match'. Returns None if not found. The UUID (not object identity) is the ONLY valid bridge between the sorted shadow-copy tree and the canonical tree.

SLICE-BASE projection for a SLICE-FROZEN Scoped Lightning Rod. Deserializes the client's durable base_render_spec (RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob) and RE-PROJECTS that scope from the /nodes-export cache into a single render TREE, so _handle_render_lightning_dom_capture can then treat it EXACTLY like a DOM captured_tree (same re-root pre-step, same build_selected_subtree_from_forest filter, same _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture compose). It REUSES the canonical funnels -- build_stage1_base_tree for a slice / slice_override scope (via the SAME nested get_slice_group_config Direction-A read the sibling _handle_render_slice_modal uses), and build_slice_subtree_from_cache(member_all=True) for a raw_root scope -- and NEVER inlines a new projection. Returns (tree, None) on success or (None, error_dict) on any failure (no tab, no group, empty group, cache miss), so the caller replies verbatim. A lightning_rod base is rejected (a prior Lightning render is already ephemeral and arrives as captured_tree, never as a durable base spec). The projected tree is a first-class EPHEMERAL dom_capture from the caller onward -- the one-way collapse of the slice, NEVER re-laundered into a durable spec. STAGE-1 POLICY THREADING (post-Sol-audit Finding 3): spec.exclude_completed and spec.descend_policy's shared anchor boundary now reach the projection -- they were silently dropped before, so a frozen scope's Scoped re-projection could surface completed nodes and descend through child anchors the original render excluded.

SCOPED LIGHTNING ROD over a FROZEN DOM view (action=render_lightning_dom_capture). The DOM-frozen half of the Scoped toggle: the dock is showing an EPHEMERAL captured DOM forest and the user fired a Lightning Rod with [Scoped] ON, so the search is confined to that on-screen forest rather than walking the whole cache root. Reads the frame's captured_tree + opaque lightning selection {mode, tags?, query?, query_mode?, match_scope, postfix_policy?}; builds the SAME singular predicate the cache path uses (build_tag_predicate / build_search_predicate) and filters the forest via build_selected_subtree_from_forest; then composes through the EXISTING _glimpse_dispatch_dom_capture machinery via its pre_filter seam, so the artifact stays a first-class kind='dom_capture' (EPHEMERAL -- the client provenance adapter must never launder it into a durable RenderProjectionSpec). gather short-circuits to gather_tags_in_forest -> render_tags_outline (raw_text/root_only), the forest sibling of the cache gather seam. No cache walk, no slice config; render_symbols is NOT supported here (it is inherently a cache-resolution mode). postfix_policy='slice' is LOUD-REJECTED in v1 (ap:IMPPTX): the full Stage-1 funnel hydrates expansions from the raw /nodes-export cache, which would silently graft nodes from OUTSIDE the ephemeral frozen domain (a source-correct forest hydrator is a separate future feature). The rejection now runs BEFORE any source-fork projection (post-Sol-audit Finding 4), so an unsupported request fails with its own actionable error -- never masked by a config/projection failure and never after wasted projection work. Task-dispatched like the sibling modal handlers. A malformed query fails LOUD (lightning_rod_query_error); an empty match renders an empty dom_capture document (valid 'no matches'), never an error.

The DOM-FROZEN sibling of _glimpse_dispatch_spec for render_spec="modal". It does NOT use the cache-projection path, because a frozen DOM view is a DIFFERENT SOURCE AXIS: an EPHEMERAL captured tree the tab pinned at freeze, not a durable /nodes-export scope. It composes that captured tree through the SAME composer + row-identity + focus primitives the cache path uses: normalize the {root,children} payload to one forest; prepare_stage2_render_forest for sort/since/counts (curated since is rejected -- no slice tags); then the shared materializer. TWO deliberate departures from the cache tail: (1) focus is EXACT-OR-ERROR -- an unresolvable focus triple returns a loud stale error, not the lenient whole-document fallback; (2) full/UUID mode is supported ONLY with headings_only=True (the {UUID<->title} harvest; a full body dump is rejected). The render_scope echo is honest kind='dom_capture' (durable_scope=False, live_gui_sync_supported=False) -- it never masquerades as raw_root/slice. GUARDRAIL: the captured tree is never folded into a RenderProjectionSpec. ADVISORY PROVENANCE (S04 Remediation Chain 4): the hard-barrier read advisory is a cache-provenance claim applied ONLY when the composed content is /nodes-export-derived -- the cache_sourced kwarg (default False, this function composes browser-captured trees) is carried explicitly to the ONE advisory authority; the render_spec="modal" dom_captured_tree read and genuinely DOM-frozen Scoped Lightning are unadvised, while a slice-frozen Scoped run passes cache_sourced=True and stays advised.

THE render_spec="modal" path -- the primary 'GLIMPSE what I'm looking at in the docked modal' capability. Issues ONE Direction-A get_current_modal_render_spec WS query to the target tab via the generic _ws_request_response rail (request_id correlation; the tab answers from its OWN dockedSliceContext.render_spec + selected-row triple -- a LEAF query, NO nested back-to-tab round trip, so NO deadlock-note applies). Deserializes the reply's render_spec blob into a RenderProjectionSpec via from_render_spec_blob (the SAME normalizer every entry point uses), applies UUID prefix-grace to every UUID in the spec (root + focus triple) via _grace_resolve_spec_uuids against the /nodes-export cache, then dispatches by kind through _glimpse_dispatch_spec -> the existing focused-projection helpers. DETERMINISTIC end-to-end: the agent types ZERO UUIDs (the blob comes from the tab's own server-adopted scope), and SERVER code (not the agent) deserializes + re-projects, so this is the (b)-variant architecture Dan chose -- the Python composer stays the sole renderer, no client-string round-trips through the server. Fails loudly if the tab has no cache-sourced render to report (success:false + a clear message telling the human to Apply a slice / push a scope first).

THE ONE agent-facing output-contract finalizer for the GLIMPSE FAMILY of MCP tools -- its consumers are the glimpse family (workflowy_glimpse), lightning_rod, anchor.dock.render, and slice_group render/sift/merge.render. Given the rich internal result dict every render helper builds, it delivers to the AGENT exactly what the human wants to see -- and nothing redundant. Rule: (1) output_file set -> pass the file-write summary through unchanged (the disk write is the deliverable, not the string). (2) result is not a dict -> already a bare value, pass through. (3) MARKDOWN / RAW-TEXT mode -- a RENDERED TEXT STRING is present -> return it RAW (real newlines, like read_text_file), NOTHING ELSE: preview_markdown (every Markdown-mode render across GLIMPSE live-DOM / slice_group / raw root_uuid / render_spec modal+blob / dom_capture, AND Lightning Rod render_tags/render_search/render_symbols) OR preview_text (the Lightning Rod gather raw-text tag outline, byte-identical to the modal's Gather). The rendered string IS the whole semantic payload in this mode, so no envelope is wanted. This is the single future-proof seam: ANY future raw-text mode just fills preview_text (or preview_markdown) and is delivered raw with ZERO further change here. (4) FULL / UUID mode -- a preview_tree is present -> return the STRUCTURED DICT, preserving preview_tree AND all the genuinely-useful metadata (node_count, depth, _source, render_scope, since_applied, ...), but STRIPPING ONLY the redundant CONTENT twins: `rows` (modal tree-view metadata that duplicates preview_tree) and any stray preview_markdown/preview_text; additionally, when headings_only=True (the compact UUID-harvest pass), strip bulky live-DOM raw `root`/`children` to keep the payload small. Full mode is for structural / UUID work, so the stats ARE wanted here -- only the duplicative rows/markdown clutter is dropped. (5) everything else (errors success:false, push_to_modal acks, gather's structured tag list when preview_text is somehow absent, empty payloads with neither field) -> pass the structured dict through unchanged so failures/acks still signal correctly. The rich internal payloads (rows, render_scope, since_applied, node_count) are LEFT INTACT on the helper returns -- they still flow to the browser/modal WS reply handlers that need them; this finalizer only shapes the AGENT-facing tool return. preview_markdown is checked before preview_text before preview_tree: at most one is ever populated on a given result, so order is belt-and-suspenders. STALE-FOCUS GUARD [ap:XDVDRG]: a Markdown/raw-text result that carries focus_unresolved is NEVER delivered raw -- its always-empty string would read as a legitimately empty view; the structured stale payload is returned instead (success flipped to false, the empty preview twins and modal rows dropped, error + focus_unresolved kept) so the shared family error boundary surfaces the loud stale-focus error. A legitimate empty (empty since-window, no focus_unresolved) still returns its raw '' when NO recency selection is active -- the (empty) stub then fires at the public funnel (9a); when a recency selection IS active ([ap:TVIIBN] 4e), the Markdown body is passed through the ONE empty-output stub (stub_empty_text_result, caveat C1) and the result opens with ONE '> Recency selection: ...' rule line naming what was chosen and teaching that sort_direction only orders (the structured full/UUID twin carries the same sentence as a top-level recency_header key, no quote marker). The header text is composed ONLY by _recency_header_sentence -- one composer, no second header writer; the browser modal / push / file paths never pass through here and are untouched by construction.

Pure simple-form identity interpretation over caller-injected cache/config operands. Reuses the existing node/group resolvers and Dock classifier, and the two pure decisions; returns a lowering or read_note intent, never acquires state or renders. Transport and note-read control flow stay per origin.

ONE estate entry through the EXISTING server render funnel (no new render path): a named-group entry normalizes via normalize_from_glimpse_args(group_id=<handle>, match_scope='name') — a slice spec at the group's stored root with its saved default sort/policy, resolved by the SAME _resolve_slice_group_handle glimpse(group_handle=…) uses; a spec entry deserializes via RenderProjectionSpec.from_render_spec_blob (spec VERBATIM, focus included), rides the UUID prefix-grace, then the loud focus-intent-loss check (a saved selection that collapses to None aborts the entry rather than dumping the whole scope). Both go through the ONE override+guard seam (_apply_modal_view_overrides_and_guard → with_view_overrides) and _glimpse_dispatch_spec — which honors single-row AND mode='rows' covering-subtree focus via the shared Stage-2 tail, and NEVER runs the in-band Anchor-Dock raw-dump guard (every estate entry passes as allow_anchor_dock=true by construction). Returns a flat per-entry record; every failure shape (invalid entry, unresolvable group, root_not_in_cache, stale focus, guard rejection, funnel error, unexpected exception) is a LOUD record — the caller keeps rendering the others. Chain-1 r2 (F5/R2-W1): ArchivedNodeReadOnlyError is the one re-raised exception — an entry whose root names a visible archived node refuses the WHOLE sink call with the universal envelope, never an isolated failed row an assembly could write into a delivery-success file.

Estate OUTPUT origin: simple forms/full JSON directly or a Dock/estate handle, interpreted by the pure grammar and injected-snapshot resolver. Dock first (no note read), else ONE live _node_read_impl; entries never nest. Lowered entries use the same TWO-branch _glimpse_estate_render_entry and _glimpse_dispatch_spec. Existing alias/title headings, scope echoes, per-entry isolation, view overrides, output_file and reserved tabs semantics remain; no renderer, wire, cache writer or transport fork. Chain 1 r2 (WO [ap:4Q3LQV] W1): under repository_view the estate delivers the ONE coherence advisory authority's warning on its own reply -- the canonical line on the screen (text adapter on the document part, below the composed '> ' lines) and the structured key on the successful file acknowledgement -- while every file byte and assembled D stays clean; applicability rides the operation's captured status and is byte-identical when clean or with the flag off.

GLIMPSE ingress: modal sentinel first; simple forms use the pure grammar and snapshot resolver before the existing spec/grace/view-override/push/render path. Explicit scope truth table and low-level defaults remain unchanged. [ap:EPR86W] part a: the raw-root cell honours recursive=False (root + direct children only, via the ONE shared walker's max_depth gate) and threads it to the push funnel; recursive=False on a slice-group scope or a live-DOM GLIMPSE is refused loudly at the boundary (and, for blobs, at the ONE spec normalizer).
yaml.role: glimpse(output_file, as_markdown: bool, target_tab, sort_by, sort_direction, slice_group, root_uuid, headings_only, render_spec, allow_anchor_dock)

yaml.comment: Server helper: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and fetch the target tab's extension settings, returning normalized (note_session_tags, global_tags, default_parent). Fails loudly if no tab is reachable. Shared by both note-session MCP tools. Archive Reads U3: the raw reply ALSO feeds remember_archive_folder_from_reply — the daemon's memory of the extension's archive_folder option, so archive reads never need a tab (the file write defers inside an augmented operation, Axiom 5/E36).

Extract the configured LOCAL-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply, defaulting to [DEFAULT_LOCAL_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('local') when absent/empty/malformed. The ONE server-side place the local-postfix default lives -- the Dock-favorites unit added the exact siblings _favorite_anchor_postfixes_from_reply / _deprecated_anchor_postfixes_from_reply and the ONE aggregator _anchor_postfix_kwargs_from_reply, so list_anchors and every classify/boundary call site read the full family vocabulary identically (no per-site defaulting, no drift). Rides in the raw reply (note_session_local_postfixes) rather than a widened _resolve_note_session_config tuple, to avoid an arity change across every existing unpack site.

Extract the configured FAVORITE-anchor postfix word list from a get_extension_settings raw reply (note_session_favorite_postfixes), defaulting to [DEFAULT_FAVORITE_ANCHOR_POSTFIX] ('fav') when absent/empty/malformed -- the exact sibling of _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply (trim, strip one leading '#', drop non-strings/empties, order-preserving de-dup). The ONE server-side place the favorite-postfix default lives, so an extension that never sends the new key keeps working unchanged (I8: no vocabulary hardcoded in behaviour; words come from the reply through this helper).

Server helper for the slice-group MCP tools: acquire the live WS peer (grace wait) and read the target tab's LIVE slice-group config via client.get_slice_group_config -> returns (groups, active_id, postfixes_dict, global_never_expand, raw). Fails loudly if no tab. The server is the single settings reader (one source of truth), exactly like _resolve_note_session_config for anchors.

CFGOP1: the ONE nested get_slice_group_config TRANSPORT for the SIX browser-facing handlers/helpers that read the live slice-group/postfix config (_handle_compile_slice_search, _handle_f8_expansion_plan, _handle_render_slice_modal's slice cell + Lightning render_tags postfix_policy='slice' branch + render_symbols suppression read, and _project_slice_base_tree_for_scoped_lightning). Consolidates the six hand-duplicated blocks (ws-acquire -> _ws_request_response('get_slice_group_config', target_endpoint_id=ORIGINATING tab, tab_optional for the endpoint-absent case, 15s) -> unknown_endpoint ghost catch -> per-site error envelope) into ONE Stage-0 transport helper. Per the STAGE-0 DOCTRINE: transport/interpretation envelopes consolidate, control flow NEVER does -- each caller keeps its own group resolution, operand parsing (parse_slice_policy_config), and reply shape. The WSLIVE2 ghost rail is PRESERVED exactly: route by the originating tab's real endpoint_id (never degraded to unknown_target_tab masking); a ghost surfaces as code='unknown_endpoint' so the client retries after the broker's re-register broadcast. context = the caller's verb-phrase (error wording stays per-site); error_type (site 6's scoped_lightning_config_read_failed) folds into BOTH envelopes. Returns (reply, None) on success or (None, envelope) on any failure.

SGSORT semantic resolve-point for a slice group's effective render sort. Preserves the inviolable None-vs-'none' distinction until the live chosen group dict is in hand: Python None / JSON null inherits the group's stored default_sort_by + default_sort_direction pair; the string 'none' is explicit document order and canonicalizes direction to asc; created/modified pass through with sanitized direction. Called only at the two slice config resolve-points (_glimpse_slice_group_from_cache and _handle_render_slice_modal), so downstream render_scope/render-tail code sees only resolved wire values and never re-decides inheritance.

Advisory short-name collision detector for slice-group WRITES (create / update-rename / merge.persist). Parses the candidate full name with the ONE grammar parser and lists every OTHER leaf group whose semantic short name collides (case-insensitive); expander/category rows and empty short names never participate (they are not short-name-resolvable), and an expander CANDIDATE yields no warnings (its short name is organizational, not a resolvable handle). Non-fatal by design: the report-only result rides in the write reply as short_name_collisions so an agent learns at WRITE time that the new name will be ambiguous as a short handle (the resolver still fails loudly with colliding_ids at USE time). Pure; no I/O.

Resolve an agent-supplied slice-group id against the in-hand groups list, with the SAME hallucinated-UUID prefix backtracking used everywhere else (anchor/snippet/SCRY) via the SHARED _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback -- but with key_prefix='grp-' since group ids are 'grp-'+uuid4().hex (not in the /nodes-export cache; matched against the slice-group config instead). Returns (index, error_dict): exact id wins; else a UNIQUE prefix match is adopted silently; a MULTI prefix match returns an error with candidate ids; no match returns a not-found error. None error => index valid.

Layer-1 shared slice-group HANDLE resolver ([ap:9QK4MV] refactor; semantic short names added 2026). Resolve an agent-supplied slice_group handle against an in-hand groups list, returning (group_dict|None, error|None). Resolution order: (1) exact id; (2) unique 'grp-' prefix via _resolve_slice_group_id; (3) case-insensitive FULL stored-name match (pipe path + trailing [n] included); (4) case-insensitive semantic SHORT-name match -- the final pipe segment, index-stripped, via the ONE grammar parser parse_slice_group_name; LEAF groups only, the supplied handle participates only when it parses as a bare leaf (a trailing [n] ON THE HANDLE is tolerated), empty short names never match. At every name stage: 1 hit -> adopt; >1 -> colliding_ids error (never auto-pick); a stage-3 full-name hit outranks stage-4 short-name hits. Pure: no network/cache/I/O. This is the ONE home for 'resolve a slice-group handle' -- every render/CRUD/purge site AND the LensSpec group-atom resolver (via its raise-style adapter) route through here, so the handle grammar can never drift between surfaces.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live config from the target tab, then delegate to client.list_note_sessions (cache walk + nested-priority DFS). Exposed publicly as 'list_anchors' (anchor = the user-facing name for what the internals still call note_session).

Internal anchor listing wrapper: public list_anchors calls it with default flags; the private widget endpoint passes tree/raw/local/favorites flags. Keeps live config resolution + client.list_note_sessions delegation in one place while preserving the public MCP tool signature. favorites_only defaults to FALSE here so the legacy list_anchors tool (all flags False) is unchanged; the public anchor.dock.list default (true) lives in _anchor_dock_list_impl alone.

MCP tool: return the user's canonical/global tag vocabulary (a routing HINT, not a constraint) read from SHARED cross-tab extension config via the tab-agnostic _resolve_note_session_config path. Tab-agnostic by design — never errors under multi-tab; only fails when no tab is reachable.

MCP tool wrapper: resolve default parent + anchor tag(s) from the target tab when not passed, then delegate to client.create_note_session (single ETCH). Fails loudly with no silent root fallback. local=True -> resolve the FIRST configured local postfix (via _local_anchor_postfixes_from_reply) and pass it as local_postfix so the anchor tag becomes base--local (a LOCAL anchor: hidden from list_anchors but still a descendants boundary). Exposed publicly as 'create_anchor' with exposed kwarg anchor_tag (internals still say note_session / session_tags).

MCP tool wrapper: resolve live anchor tags from the target tab, guard the 'note session' terminology rule, then delegate to client.update_note_session (rename base name preserving tags / replace note; mapped-subtree advisory surfaced for the agent to report). Exposed publicly as 'update_anchor' (internals still say note_session).

MCP tool wrapper: validate the EXACTLY-ONE payload contract (nodes XOR note_file XOR content; loud on both/neither/all; checked FIRST, before any live config read), then delegate to client.add_to_anchor (placement-guarded ETCH). The guard (folder + non-Markdown-file rejection) is the only value-add over workflowy_etch; dialect-neutral capture primitive for anchors. note_file: absolute-path UTF-8 text file -> exactly ONE node (file stem = name, raw text = note). content: raw string with required name= -> exactly ONE node (name = NAME, content = NOTE). name: optional override with note_file (skips stem as name).
yaml.role: ⚡ add_to_anchor(parent_uuid: str, nodes, tags, target_tab, note_file, content, name)
⚡ scry(node_id: str, depth, size_limit: int, output_file, allow_anchor_dock)

yaml.comment: node.resolve: the node family's identity verb ([ap:CZ95R6], Dan's REVISED 074 ruling — per-family verbs, ONE shared implementation). Accepts any handle form (exact UUID | its 8-hex first segment | a unique longer prefix | [ap:CORE], UUID-first with the AP-ID leg on unresolved fall-through) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (which wraps the ONE prefix kernel — no second resolver), against the operation's pinned cache map, and returns the unified non-raising 0/1/N record: on a unique match the node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level ('no anchor point available' in words when the node carries none), every candidate row carrying its vocabulary on ambiguity. A resolve is for citations/records — never needed before an ordinary handle call: every handle parameter already accepts all the forms directly.

node.ancestors: the extension's F3 ancestor chain as a real MCP verb — 'where does this node live in the full document, and is it inside a mapped file/folder?'. Pure cache read through the existing operation boundary (NO new transport): resolve handle against the pinned snapshot, walk + compose via ancestor_path.build_ancestor_path_document (the ONE core the F3/F2 WS handler delegates to, so the two homes can never drift; the WS frame-sending _resolve_uuid_path_and_respond is NEVER called from here), Dock-marker vocabulary via the ONE established Direction-A config read (skipped entirely when markers=false). detail='compact' returns the raw Markdown document (key line + chain + → uuid tail); detail='full' adds structured rows (title/tags/dock flags/completed/map_state/metrics + ap_id via the ONE shared leading-AP splitter) beside the same markdown.

LIGHTNING ROD public MCP tool. Thin wrapper over the internal _lightning_rod_from_cache orchestrator: rate-limit acquire, then dispatch. Modes: gather (discover tags under a root -> feeds render_tags), render_tags (Option-B prefix-family tag filter; NO deprecation/suppress/expand semantics by DEFAULT -- the opt-in postfix_policy='slice' (ap:IMPPTX) instead routes it through the FULL Stage-1 funnel build_stage1_base_tree with the live postfix words + the real f8_global_never_expand_tags list), render_search (shlex 'smart' boolean/glob OR 'regex' free-text filter), render_symbols (dynamic tag-free beacon slice from a UUID/symbol/AP-ID list). Mutation modes: ensure_beacons/remove_beacon_tags (Q3 DISK beacons) and mutate_node_tags (Q4 batch Workflowy #tag add/remove/rename on NODES by UUID/[ap:CORE] handle -- operations-only; a thin ledger wrapper over the per-node tag primitives). Render modes are cache-only; no WebSocket (except one postfix config read for render_tags 'slice'), no slice-group persistence, no Workflowy-UI. Shared render knobs mirror glimpse and flow through render_stage2_filter_sort. since='curated' rejected (no slice tag set); live-GUI-sync never supported. The traversal pair rides the shared selection fragment ([ap:EPR86W] 4b): the walking verbs (gather/render_tags/render_search) carry recursive+descend_policy, and recursive=False is refused LOUDLY at the top of this body -- before the push branch, so a pushed selection cannot silently drop the request (one refusal text with the orchestrator's backstop, _lightning_recursive_refusal). The grammar docstring here is the AGENT-FACING interface (the caller is an LLM building the query from natural language, so it is small+explicit+deterministic with normative examples). PUSH-TO-MODAL: push_to_modal=True + target_tab route through the SAME _glimpse_push_slice_to_modal channel the GLIMPSE tool uses (the 4th push scope cell -> apply_slice_in_dock carrying a `lightning` scope -> the ONE shared applySliceGroupIntoDock apply path), so a pushed Lightning Rod render is identical to a ribbon-triggered one; as_markdown/output_file are inapplicable to a push (returns a small ack, not content). Only the injected predicate (or, under postfix_policy='slice', the shared funnel) differs from the other cache-projection + push scopes -- the same universal pipeline.
yaml.role: ⚡ lightning_rod(mode, root_uuid, tags, query, query_mode, tag_match, postfix_policy, as_markdown, sort_by, sort_direction, headings_only, since, output_file)

yaml.comment: Canonical Node-family ETCH front. Selects the existing synchronous or asynchronous ETCH primitive, standardizes sync mutation acknowledgements, and converts async legacy job handles into the shared family job envelope without changing ETCH payload semantics.

Canonical Tag-family batch front. Reuses the one Q4 operations normalizer and the existing preflight-all-then-commit Lightning Rod tag orchestrator, preserving its complete ledger and batch-gating semantics.

Node-as-a-file paged grep front: single-node search delegates to the existing ONE live read and decoder; subtree search consumes the operation-pinned canonical map and established ordered scope walker, never live publisher state or per-descendant GETs, and hides completed nodes (plus their descendants) by default -- the dock.peek/render default; include_completed opts back in; suppressed nodes and child Docks stay included (search is a grep). The query is the ONE span matcher compile_note_query; the report is the ONE compact grep formatter search_note_documents (ripgrep-style rows, match_width/context_width crops, occurrences in the footer), which also owns the all-caps pagination banner that opens every multi-page report (the Source line rides the formatter's header_line slot, below the banner); each call uses the standard family boundary/finalizer for adoption and advisories. _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by orders the node groups; recent='last N'/'newest N' keeps the N newest matching NODES by resolve_item_count_basis -- trimmed ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes distinct from the matched-line cap; ranking is dock_peek_metrics.apply_dock_peek_recency, the ONE idiom) to the ONE _normalize_note_grep_params; node.search/anchor.search/sift schemas share _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too -- through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30, no third producer). The plan keeps literal/regex query compilation and the report tail (_note_grep_report) stays shared with anchor.search. No retained snapshot, cache writes, transport fork, or renderer.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Node family. Thin handlers re-front lifecycle primitives, node-as-a-file read/search, and AP-aware leading-emoji mutations while the registry remains the sole authority for canonical verbs, role-named handles, transition aliases, schemas, effects, async metadata, and describe output.
Config-only Slice Group deletion. Resolves through the shared id/prefix/name resolver, clears active_group_id atomically when needed, persists once, and never touches Workflowy tags.

Recursive LensSpec merge persistence orchestrator. Evaluates once against the immutable S06 T1 snapshot, materializes the authoritative tree, preflights reproducibility/identity/collisions, reuses the shipped plan-simulate-Q4-verify compiler, then performs a fresh T2 config identity check and atomic create/reuse update.

Shared low-level/group-aware purge apply orchestrator. Recomputes and fingerprint-gates the preview, refuses shared families by default, delegates exact removals to Q4, rebuilds the eager-patched cache, and verifies no mutable family occurrence remains.

Assembly point for the consolidated public Tag family. Six operations preserve surgical single-node primitives, the complete batch ledger, and the fingerprint-gated purge workflow while the registry owns canonical verbs, aliases, schemas, effects, and describe output.

Shared Anchor-Dock root guard behind the two IN-BAND full-dump returns (node.scry and the bare-root_handle glimpse raw dump). Resolves the handle (UUID / unique prefix / [ap:CORE]) and classifies the root node's NAME tags against ONE welded snapshot (the resolver's echoed cache map + ONE live Dock-vocabulary read, optionally injected so the stop_at_child_anchors boundary shares it). Verdicts: root IS an Anchor Dock (global or local) -> raise _AnchorDockRootDetected with a peek/render teaching message; root ABSENT from the cache -> raise _FullDumpRootCacheMiss (FAIL CLOSED -- an unclassifiable in-band full-dump root is refused, never allowed to fall through to the API subtree fetch; the message points at system.cache.refresh); otherwise return {resolved, anchor_vocabulary} so the caller's downstream resolution and boundary predicate reuse the same operands. The live extension-settings WS read is FIRST-CLASS (the historical 'scry never touches the WebSocket' doctrine is retracted: node CONTENTS come from the cache/API, the Dock-tag VOCABULARY from the tab; a failed config read is loud, never a silent skip). Out-of-band deliveries (output_file, push_to_modal) are exempt by caller placement, never by this helper; allow_anchor_dock=true skips the guard wholesale at each caller.

Pure six-character uppercase-base36 AP-ID generator. Retries against an injected collision predicate and fails loudly after the bounded attempt budget; allocation locking and reservation live in the caller.

Pure compact Dock-peek serializer. One globally padded AP-only column over visible rows; blank for missing APs, no column if none. Names are shown in full (trailing #tags included) -- max_chars is an opt-in middle-ellipsis budget, 0/None = unlimited. The Dock's own '> …' description excerpt is budgeted SEPARATELY (max_description_chars, default 256, CF-MST-015; the name budget never touches it and show_description=false still suppresses it entirely). Only the trimmed body indents (four spaces per real node depth) and only while the rows are the plain document-order walk: a recent-N selection or a timestamp sort renders FLAT (a timestamp order is not a tree order), and UTAERZ shows the nesting per row there instead -- one ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint (the parent's [ap:CORE], else its short UUID) on every row whose parent is not the peeked Dock (parent_handles is the impl's precomputed map; depth stays in the JSON). The header names the selection/order, including 'N completed hidden' whenever the default completed-exclusion removed rows (recency views AND the plain inventory alike, U6/J11); under a recent-N selection [ap:TVIIBN] 4e adds ONE explicit rule line directly below the header (describe_dock_peek_recency_rule, the peek-side twin of the render verbs' _recency_header_sentence): sort_direction only orders the selected rows, it never changes which rows were chosen. Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row; both route through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over the caller's uuid_prefix_collisions index (CF-22/O3), never a second shortener. Four source metrics and Dock/favorite/local/completed flags (marker order ⚓ ⭐ Ⓛ ✓; ⭐ only on a Dock row) with a policy-aware legend. No acquisition, source mutation, document rendering or traversal decisions.
yaml.role: ƒ _render_dock_peek_raw_text(dock_name, root_note, rows, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, max_description_chars, root_metrics, recursive, descend_policy, selection, sort, root_uuid, uuid_prefix_collisions, parent_handles)

yaml.comment: Pure compact serializer for slice_group.list: one raw-text nested outline of the persisted slice groups. Rows come from build_slice_group_display_items -- the exact Python twin of the client's buildNestedDisplayItems (auto-vivified synthetic categories, the lowest-indexed canonical expander owning descendants, duplicate expander rows marked ' ⚠ duplicate category', null-index-last case-insensitive ordering, every category expanded). Category rows are bare '▾ name' (organizational; no ID, and hidden category-group tags are never exposed); leaf rows are '[<bare 8-hex group prefix>] short-name — up to 4 #tags (+N more) ✅' (✅ on the active group only). The header counts every stored record and ends detail='full' for JSON. Pure; no I/O.

Anchor Dock inventory front. detail='compact' (THE default everywhere -- consolidated registry, impl, and the legacy list_anchors delegate) returns ONE raw-text inventory string from one _list_anchors_internal(tree_view=True) acquisition, serialized by the ONE shared _render_anchor_tree_raw_text compact mode; detail='full' is the explicit escape hatch returning the established structured payload (rows gain is_favorite; the favorites echo keys ride along). favorites_only defaults TRUE HERE (the public shortlist default; _list_anchors_internal and the legacy tool stay False): the ⭐ favorites shortlist with the zero-favorites fallback, compact header counts taken from the echoed shown_global_count/shown_local_count so the arithmetic is correct under favorites. Row descriptions ([ap:YLHDIN] part 2): every compact row carries the Dock's FIRST description line as a ' — excerpt' tail (show_description=true default; max_description_chars budgets it, default 120, 0 hides; the same metadata-stripped text the structured rows carry). An inventory serializer, never a document render: no RenderProjectionSpec, no Stage 1/2, no composer.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_list_impl(include_local, target_tab, detail, max_chars, favorites_only, max_description_chars, show_description)

yaml.comment: Dock-create front: description is OPTIONAL (VBIKIZ) and defaults to empty -- the registry (not this impl) owns the name=topic / note=description aliases via param_aliases. Creates via client.create_note_session, so no tag-write path exists.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_create_impl(topic, description, parent_handle, local, extra_tags, target_tab, favorite)

yaml.comment: Atomic Dock update front. All name work goes through _node_edit_core + the ONE protected-name composer from ONE live GET snapshot (title, AP-ID, and the tag list the attribute transform rewrites never mix cache/live). Topic follows the public protected-name rules (supplied tags/AP changes rejected) and preserves the Dock's existing leading emoji run (Z8Q0PF+LITF2F: the caller need not pass an emoji; a supplied topic run wins explicitly; replace_emoji=True hands the run to the supplied topic wholesale -- its run replaces the existing one, its absence clears it; the SAME composed name is computed for the no-op/name_changed verdict and the write, so the two composer calls can never disagree); explicit local/favorite attribute writes are the ONLY tag rewrite, delivered via the narrow _tag_transform channel as a per-FAMILY set/unset-ONE-attribute transform (I6/I7): for each targeted family it removes ONLY that family's proper tags and re-inserts one canonical tag per remaining attribute (fixed order local, favorite; existing words preserved; bare base when the last attribute is unset -- Dock identity is never deleted), leaving every other family's tags, every --deprecated tag, every unknown-postfix tag and every unrelated tag byte-for-byte in place. NEVER canonicalises to base_tags[0] (the old family-switch bug). families= names the family to write when the node carries more than one (dock_families_ambiguous otherwise; a family without a proper tag on the node is dock_family_not_on_node; --deprecated-only does not count as present). Zero writes on any validation error. One live GET, at most one write.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_update_impl(dock_handle, topic, description, local, target_tab, favorite, families)

yaml.comment: anchor.dock.get_description: the Dock-description getter (TODO [ap:YLHDIN] part 1, Dan's "get description") as a thin Dock-checked PRESET over the ONE metadata header -- it resolves against the pinned cache, checks Dock-hood with the same classify_anchor_tags matcher the dock mutation verbs use (a non-Dock is a loud not_an_anchor_dock teaching error pointing at anchor.point.read), counts DIRECT child Docks through build_dock_peek_index's priority-ordered child lists classified by the ONE boundary predicate (build_anchor_boundary_predicate), then delegates to _anchor_point_read_impl with extra_header_lines=("child docks: N",) -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs; no second metadata header exists. The description (the note) rides the getter UNGUARDED and untruncated: fetching the description is the point (dock.peek's compact excerpt budgets it at 256 and detail='full' carries it whole -- the same norm). The vocabulary read fails loudly with no Workflowy tab (dock.peek's rule): the Dock check itself needs it. Pure read.

Dock-peek read-only inventory front: existing one config read/resolver/pinned map and owned source-metrics index. Direct children remain default; recursive=true uses real node depth and stops at nested Docks unless descend_policy='all' explicitly opens them (global and local alike). Rows carry the FULL node name verbatim (trailing #tags included; title/tags split alongside), the item's own created_at/modified_at, and parent_id (UTAERZ: the walked parent, so the flat recent/timestamp compact view shows a per-row ' ← in ‹parent handle›' hint for rows whose parent is not the peeked Dock; document order keeps indentation and no hints). Row handles ([ap:0M6VP8] peek half): rows without an AP-ID show a bracketed short UUID handle in the body by default; show_ids=true adds it to every row -- both through the ONE shortener unique_short_uuid_prefix over a build_uuid_prefix_collisions index built once per call from the same pinned cache map (CF-22/O3; parent hints use the same authority, the parent's [ap:CORE] when it carries one). recent=N selects the N newest walked rows on recent_by (default modified) and sort_by/sort_direction order the whole inventory -- one pure policy (apply_dock_peek_recency) applied between the walk and BOTH renderers so compact and detail='full' select identical items; neither knob given = document order, unchanged. Completed rows are marked but HIDDEN by default on EVERY view -- recency, timestamp sort, and the plain document-order inventory alike (U6/J11; include_completed=true opts back in) -- the filter lives solely inside the policy. detail='full' additionally carries the Dock's untruncated one-line 'description'; the compact '> …' excerpt budgets it at 256 chars. Totals always cover the full subtree. No new live reads, mutation claims, cache publication, renderer or broker path.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_peek_impl(dock_handle, target_tab, detail, show_ids, show_counts, show_description, max_chars, recursive, descend_policy, recent, recent_by, sort_by, sort_direction, include_completed)

yaml.comment: anchor.search: a node.search-shaped grep scoped to ONE Anchor Dock's subtree. Acquisition is dock.peek's own pattern -- the ONE note-session config read (the live Dock vocabulary; loud with no tab, like dock.peek), the generic handle resolver, the pinned operation cache -- then the ONE generic Stage-1 walk build_selected_subtree_from_cache with member_all=True, the shared build_anchor_boundary_predicate (descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' default stops at child Docks; each child Dock's own name/note is still searched as a signpost; 'all' enters them) and exclude_completed (completed nodes hidden by default, root exempt -- node.search's own default; include_completed opts back in). Documents from _anchor_scope_documents feed the ONE shared grep tail (_note_grep_plan + _note_grep_report + note_lines.search_note_documents): query machinery identical to node.search (literal or is_regex line-local, context_lines/context_width/match_width, matched-LINE offset/max_matches paging with the all-caps banner). _note_grep_plan delegates grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls (sort_by/sort_direction/recent/recent_by/max_nodes -- node-level: recent keeps the N newest matching nodes, hidden ones counted in the footer; max_nodes caps matching nodes) to _normalize_note_grep_params; the registry takes the ONE schema fragment _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties, shared with node.search/sift/render_search. lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both owners too. match_scope ('name_and_note' default, sift's vocabulary) picks WHAT the query reads: name_and_note = note lines plus the TITLE (a title-only match renders its header row with the D6 '(title match)' marker -- the formatter drops the marker when note lines also hit); 'name' = title rows only (the document carries no note, so the shared formatter cannot leak note rows). No second formatter, second matcher, second walk, second vocabulary reader or second ranking idiom exists.

Named raw-root GLIMPSE preset for an Anchor Dock. Reuses the existing root projection/modal-push paths while mapping the public most-recent token `recent` (legacy `tail`/`since` accepted as silent aliases at the registry) to the existing SinceSpec edge. [ap:EPR86W] part a: carries the traversal pair with EXACTLY dock.peek's names and values (defaults differ by design: recursive=True, descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' -- today's behavior unchanged); recursive=False renders the Dock + its DIRECT children (child Docks and plain nodes alike) and nothing deeper, with descend_policy moot, on both the content path (max_depth=1 through the ONE shared walker) and the push path (the flag rides the pushed spec blob).
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_dock_render_impl(dock_handle, sort_by, sort_direction, recent, headings_only, as_markdown, output_file, push_to_modal, target_tab)

yaml.comment: Canonical Anchor Point capture front. Preserves all guarded add_to_anchor payload/tag behavior and optionally reserves plus injects a collision-checked AP-ID before the one ETCH, preventing post-create partial state.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_capture_impl(parent_handle, nodes, tags, target_tab, note_file, content, name, ap_id)

yaml.comment: MOVE-only single/batch note-range extraction. ONE live source snapshot and the shared note_lines planner; captures run in document order through _anchor_point_capture_impl, EVERY success/root-id acknowledgement is checked before ONE whole-note _node_edit_core call with the original snapshot injected. No direct cache edits or parallel mutation transport. Failure ledger distinguishes source-not-written from an uncertain update outcome and preserves typed coherence refusals.

Assign a collision-checked AP-ID to an existing point via the narrow _assign_ap_core channel of _node_edit_core -- the composer's assign leg preserves the existing title and trailing tags automatically (no more raw prefix-string splice). Existing IDs are never replaced; a process-local lock plus reservation ledger closes same-server allocation races.

Dedicated idempotent AP-ID removal path. Resolves the node handle before mutation (so the AP-ID itself may be used to target the node), performs one live structured read, then delegates through _node_edit_core's narrow _remove_ap_id channel using that SAME snapshot. The pure composer removes only the leading AP token while preserving leading decoration, ordinary title, trailing tags, and one-layer entity semantics. Returns the removed handle + a loud citation-invalidation warning; an AP-less node is a true no-op with zero write. The removed core is deliberately NOT released from the process-local allocation ledger -- immediate same-process reuse would make old citations resolve to the wrong node.

anchor.point.resolve: the AP-ID-first identity resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]) through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (prefer='anchor_point': the AP leg runs first, the UUID leg only on unresolved fall-through, so a UUID / 8-hex handle resolves here too and a bare base36 core that is also hex stays AP-domain first). Established 0/1/N shape preserved for the live consumers (success/match_count/candidates/resolved_ap_id), now with the unified identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level on a unique match and per candidate row ('no anchor point available' when a node carries none). Never needed before an ordinary call: every handle parameter accepts an AP-ID directly.

anchor.point.read: node.read with Anchor usability defaults — metadata header over the LIVE note through _read_live_node_note (ONE rate-limited fetch/decode) and snippet_view.render_note_body (ONE guard/window/number/exact body), with validate_note_read_lines before I/O and normalize_note_view_params at the public front. Numbered by default; guard 400, size_only = header plus size line; no output_file/as_raw_node. Header metadata still uses the resolver's echoed pinned map, walk_ancestor_chain/build_ancestor_path_document/node_timestamp, peek markers and source metrics, dates, 8-hex handle and path. Dock vocabulary still degrades VISIBLY with no tab; ✓/🗺️/📄 need no tab. Only the framing and defaults differ from node.read. extra_header_lines (internal channel, anchor.dock.get_description only) splices Dock-only lines directly under the name/metrics line -- the ONE header composer serves both verbs.
yaml.role: ⚡ _anchor_point_read_impl(node_handle, offset, limit, with_line_numbers, view, target_tab, extra_header_lines)

yaml.comment: anchor.point.touch: ordered batch, content-preserving modifiedAt advance so a chosen working set surfaces FIRST in dock.peek recent_by='modified'. handles[0] = highest priority = newest afterwards, achieved by touching in REVERSE input order, one governed write per item (~1 s each) through _node_edit_core's narrow _touch channel (layoutMode echo, name-identity fallback; never composes text). Preflight: duplicate handles (literal or same resolved UUID) = batch REFUSE, zero writes; unresolvable / not-in-cache / mapped (non-'unmapped' _classify_node_map_state -- disk is truth) / Anchor Dock (unless allow_docks) = per-item SKIP, batch continues. Execution: live GET before, write, verify content fingerprint unchanged and modifiedAt strictly increasing (one re-touch after a short sleep on a tie); an unknown write outcome, a content change or a non-advancing timestamp STOPS the batch (remaining rows not_run, never re-sent). Complete ledger in INPUT order + summary with order_established; success only when every row touched; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

anchor.point.promote: the curation pass made atomic -- batch move-with-provenance (mode: move, default) and promote-as-COPY (mode: derivative). Two grammars (items=[{handle, destination, tags?, mode?, children?}] | handles=[...] + destination + tags? + mode? + children?) normalized by the pure normalize_promote_items before any I/O. Per item: resolve handle + destination through the generic resolver against ONE pinned cache map; origin = nearest ancestor Anchor Dock (global or local; else the immediate parent) via nearest_anchor_dock_ancestor; STRUCTURAL mapped-node refusal on source AND destination (_classify_node_map_state != 'unmapped' -- stricter than capture's guard, Markdown included) plus the first-line Cartographer-metadata content check (delegated to the ONE managed-metadata registry, managed_metadata.py). Batch grammar modelled on beacon.tags.ensure: per-item SKIP (unresolvable, not in cache, mapped) continues; batch REFUSE with zero writes (malformed, duplicate handles literal or same resolved UUID, destination inside the source's own subtree); STOP on any ambiguous post-send outcome (remaining rows not_run, nothing re-sent). MOVE = _node_move_impl(src, dest, 'bottom') + ONE _node_edit_core(note=trail+old, _tag_transform=add, _current_node=live) = 2 governed writes; the trail line '↩ moved from <origin> (<uuid8>) · <date>' is plain text, newest on top. MANAGED METADATA ([ap:BNNUZ4]): a note carrying a recognised managed block (program_interface YAML, estate payloads, manifests, snapshot/ledger names, … -- detect_trail_skip_metadata over the registry) STILL moves/copies but writes NO trail line: the move path skips the trail write (tags-only edit when tags are wanted, zero second writes otherwise; trail_written stays false) and the derivative path bakes no '↩ derived from' line; the row's info field names the kind and row["trail_line"] keeps the would-be line for provenance. DERIVATIVE = ONE subtree ETCH (_node_etch_sync_impl) built from the pinned cache with a fresh AP core reserved for the root and every AP-bearing descendant BEFORE the create (zero transient duplicate AP-IDs), decoded wire text, the '↩ derived from … · source [ap:X] <uuid8>' line baked into the root note and the tags into the root name; completed descendants skipped unless include_completed (then re-completed after the create via list_nodes + complete_node); children:false copies the root alone; the source is never written. ARCHIVED SOURCE (U2, Axiom 6/G8): a derivative's source may be an archived node -- the one sanctioned copy that reads archived content: move skips it with the §5.2.1 + how-to-copy story (reason archived_node, archive provenance on the row), derivative copies the archive file's VERBATIM records via ArchiveStore.verbatim_subtree_records (original names/parents/priorities, no 📦, no marker; text served verbatim, never re-decoded, E7), mints fresh AP-IDs, names the ARCHIVE as the trail-line origin ('↩ derived from archive "name" (basename, exported date) · date · source <uuid8>'), never installs an overlay, never touches the file; an archived DESTINATION refuses with §5.2.3 as a skipped row. Ledger in input order + summary; success only when every row landed; partial_success on mixed outcomes.

yaml.comment: Assembly point for the public Anchor family. Re-fronts Dock/Point primitives, verified-before-delete range extraction, bounded peek/render presets, the Dock-scoped grep (anchor.search -- the ONE shared note-grep tail over a Dock boundary walk), and collision-checked AP-ID allocation while the registry remains the sole dispatch/describe/schema/effects authority.

The one pure Stage-0 normalizer for the opaque Lightning render_lens selection. Parses the recursive LensSpec, makes query/query_mode/match_scope defaults explicit (an omitted match_scope defaults name-only for a recipe render, name_and_note for a sift query), and preserves path-bearing LensSpecError failures for every ingress surface.

Immutable Lens Stage-0 bundle welding the pure LensEvalContext to the exact cache mapping, copied group/config operands, active-group id, and raw config reply used for one projection. MCP and modal origins retain distinct transport rails but converge on this one snapshot shape.

The one transport-free Lens Stage-0 interpreter. It parses an already-read config reply, captures or accepts exactly one cache mapping, builds snapshot-backed group/root resolvers plus the Anchor Dock boundary, and returns the immutable _LensStage0Snapshot consumed by both MCP and modal origins.

Compatibility context-only seam over the MCP-origin Lens Stage-0 snapshot builder. Performs the existing one config read through _build_lens_stage0_snapshot and returns only its pure LensEvalContext for callers/tests that need the engine operand directly.

Transport-free shared LensSpec projection core. Both the MCP family path and the docked-modal handler inject one already-read Lens Stage-0 snapshot, then reuse this single normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift implementation so canonical adoption, leaf algebra, and cache identity cannot drift. Threads the surface match_scope as the default for lens atoms that omit their own (recipe render = the surface value, default name-only; sift = 'name' for tag atoms while the query keeps its own name_and_note scope). A sift query returns sift_predicate -- the ONE build_search_predicate instance that decided the sifted tree -- so the MCP grep tier classifies its documents with the SAME predicate. The result ALWAYS carries lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY]): lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids receives the final tree, per-atom resolved roots AND the SAME pinned cache, so only strict input-root ancestors outside every member region become scaffold even when an input root is absent from the final tree. Every lens tail forwards this set to the existing materializer cause; ancestor_notes is folded producer-side. No second suppression path.

Thin MCP-origin consumer of the shared render_lens projector. It performs the ordinary tab-agnostic config read, builds one Lens Stage-0 snapshot, delegates normalize/evaluate/materialize/sift to _project_render_lens_from_cache, then uses the shared Stage-2 render/file tail -- EXCEPT under the sift grep tier ([ap:47B7WO], grep_params set by slice_group.sift tier='context'): the branch after projection bypasses the Stage-2 composer and returns the ONE compact grep formatter's report over exactly the lens's admitted nodes, so selection is never re-decided and the report is node.search's shape by construction. Grep values/defaults/bounds AND the [ap:O3MDOY] match controls are owned by _normalize_note_grep_params and the schemas by _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties; lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' (5c, [ap:2EG7TD]) calls both too, through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30). max_nodes ([ap:O3MDOY] half 2) caps the headings tier: it rides the Stage-2 call with the lens's sift_predicate so the cap counts only MATCHING nodes AFTER the sort and the since prune (selection -> order -> cap). lens_scaffold_ids ([ap:I506WY], unit 5g) rides the Stage-2 call too -- the projection's lens_scaffold_ids (the connective scaffolding above the input roots, lens_engine.lens_scaffold_ancestor_ids) forwarded so that ancestor path renders headings-only even in document order; the spec's ancestor_notes opt-out folds HERE (producer-side, like the chronological boolean's fold): an overridden render passes nothing and stays byte-identical.

Slice Group registry and existing render-recipe origin. Render/sift/merge.render lower simple forms through ONE pure grammar and snapshot interpretation before the unchanged render_lens pipeline; formal lens requests and merge.persist retain their grammar. Schemas/describe/errors remain registry-owned; recipe match_scope defaults name, sift query defaults name_and_note. Render/sift/merge.render return through _shape_glimpse_family_return: raw Markdown by default, the structured result without rows when as_markdown=false. Sift's tier 'context' (the default, [ap:47B7WO]) branches AFTER projection: the ONE grep formatter reports line hits over the lens's admitted nodes; tier 'headings' keeps the tree render; push_to_modal is headings-tier only. _normalize_note_grep_params is the ONE grep value/default/bound owner AND the ONE owner of the [ap:O3MDOY] node-level match controls (sort_by/sort_direction/recent/recent_by/max_nodes -- active on BOTH sift tiers; on 'context' at node level through _render_sift_grep_result, on 'headings' the render semantics plus the max_nodes cap through the Stage-2 tail), and _note_grep_properties + _search_match_controls_properties are the ONE schema fragments shared with node.search/anchor.search/render_search; lightning_rod.render_search's tier 'context' ([ap:2EG7TD], landed) calls both too, through the SAME _render_sift_grep_result tail (CF-30). [ap:I506WY] (unit 5g): render/sift/merge.render all expose ancestor_notes -- on a lens render the flag restores the LENS-SCAFFOLD notes (the connective scaffolding above the input roots renders heading-only by default, even in document order; the projection computes lens_scaffold_ids, the lens tail forwards it, the materializer owns the cause), besides its U6 chronological meaning.

The ONE global-suppression list read for every beacon SYMBOL resolution (beacon.resolve, beacon.snippet symbol leg and the symbol fallback of a UUID-shaped handle, legacy snippet tools, beacon.tags.ensure/remove, and -- via resolve_node_handle's suppress_tags_provider -- the tag.add/remove/rename and node-mutator symbol legs). Dan's ruling [ap:7ORCPL].

THE UUID-shaped-handle gate for the beacon source_handle (snippet/resolve + the shared snippet body): True when the handle — after ONE pass through the shared bracket unwrapper unwrap_bracketed_uuid_handle — is a hyphen-normalized pure-hex string of >= 8 chars (the shared prefix kernel's min_prefix_len floor, i.e. a full UUID or any of its prefixes down to the 8-hex first segment, bracketed forms included). Resolution itself is NOT done here: the gate only routes to the UUID leg, which resolves through the ONE shared kernel _resolve_uuid_with_prefix_fallback (via resolve_uuid_like_node_handle / beacon_get_code_snippet); a symbol that happens to be 8+ hex chars still resolves on the symbol fallback. [ap:G5C9BX]: widened from the old >= 32-char rule that made beacon.snippet refuse the 8-hex segment its own describe recommends.

Unified S08 live source reader behind beacon.snippet. UUID-shaped handles (full UUID or 8-hex segment, via the shared gate _looks_like_uuid_source_handle) keep the forgiving UUID-first/symbol-fallback posture ([ap:G5C9BX]; a colliding prefix surfaces as a loud did-you-mean, never a guess); source symbols use the existing client resolver with retry-without-file_path. root_handles ([ap:WB323O]) resolves through _resolve_beacon_scope_roots (fail loud on an unresolvable root) and scopes the SYMBOL leg only -- candidates outside every root are dropped before the 0/1/N decision, so a duplicate symbol in another repository or a file copy resolves instead of colliding; an explicit UUID source_handle is read as given. Resolves live with context=0 (no engine padding — context is a render-layer knob), then returns the numbered, length-guarded snippet view from snippet_view.render_snippet_view.

The beacon identity resolve ([ap:CZ95R6]) behind beacon.resolve, through the ONE shared resolve_node_identity_record (prefer='symbol', with server.py's _looks_like_uuid_source_handle passed as the family's uuid_shaped_gate): the symbol leg stays first for symbol-shaped handles (suppress list + root_handles scope honoured, read lazily ONLY when the symbol leg actually runs so a UUID- or AP-shaped resolve never needs a connected tab), with U1's landed gates — a UUID-shaped handle (full UUID or 8-hex segment) routes to the uuid leg first (a colliding prefix is a loud N-candidate record, never a guess, never a symbol fallback; only fully-unresolved falls through to symbols) and an explicitly AP-shaped handle ([ap:CORE] / ap:CORE / [CORE]) routes to the AP leg first, with AP also the last fall-through for everything else. Returns the unified non-raising 0/1/N record: on a unique match the resolved node's full identifier vocabulary {short, uuid, ap_id} at the top level plus the symbol descriptor fields (resolved_symbol / resolved_symbol_kind / scope_filtered_count passthroughs); every candidate row carries its vocabulary. root_handles ([ap:WB323O]) resolves through _resolve_beacon_scope_roots (fail loud on an unresolvable root) and scopes the SYMBOL leg only; the UUID and AP legs ignore the scope, exactly as they ignore #wfy-suppress.

Assembly point for the render-only progressive-disclosure Lightning Rod family. Five tight schemas dissolve the legacy mode mega-schema while every handler fixes one mode and delegates to the one hoisted legacy authority. render_nodes ([ap:OSQHRG]) is render_symbols NAMED FOR NODES: without root_handles it resolves every item as a NODE via the ONE shared resolve_uuid_or_anchor_point_handle and defaults the scope to the resolved nodes themselves (a {symbol} item or an unresolvable string refuses loud -- symbols need root_handles), then delegates to the ONE render_symbols path, so the wire still carries mode=render_symbols (no new lightning mode, no extension change). S04 MCP dispatch hooks injected into every family front: result finalizer applies the ONE standardized hard-barrier read advisory to cache-backed read-safe non-render-family results (render families are covered at their internal cache-render seams, which also covers modal delivery); mutation admission classifies each spec and runs the fresh LOCKED hard-stop gate only for refuse-class operations, returning the universal coherence_barrier_active envelope; the exception mapper keeps typed coherence refusals from collapsing into operation_failed. 23db916f: the finalizer ALSO drains the per-operation handle-correction echo state first (handle_corrections) and applies it to EVERY family -- one 'resolved: <short> <name> (corrected from <supplied>)' line prefixed to string results, a top-level resolved_corrections list on dict results -- BEFORE the advisory, so a prefixed result reads advisory -> correction line -> body; the render-family and cache-back guards govern only the advisory, never the echo.

S04 §7.5 MCP result finalizer + Archive Reads U2 banner order + U3 footer: the coherence layers run first (handle-correction echo, then the ONE hard-barrier read advisory on cache-backed read-safe non-render results), then the archive steps — the §5.5 FOOTER first (fallback-mode success of one of the 16 flag verbs: \n + the line as the LAST string line, archives_left_out on dicts, counted from the overlay's precomputed planted chains), and the ARCHIVE BANNER drains LAST (§5.1), applied as the finalizer's final step so the ⚠️⚠️⚠️ ARCHIVED NODE line is the FIRST line of the result, above the advisory and above every resolved: correction line, on EVERY family (the two render families included: their internal seams advise, the banner still drains here). Strings gain the banner line(s) (one per archive file that answered, first-answered order) prefixed above the body; dicts gain archive_warning + archived; a PYDANTIC MODEL result (Chain-1 W1/F1: the archived structured node.read) is delivered as its own by-alias field mapping plus the same two keys, so an archive-answered structured read can never escape the warning; operations where no archive answered and nothing was left out are byte-identical.

THE injected operation_invoker every family front passes to dispatch_operation (§4.3): classifies the operation ONCE per call with _archive_mode_for (include on include_archives:true for reads; fallback for reads — ON since U2 (_ARCHIVE_FALLBACK_ENABLED); none with reason write/export/purge_preview/beacon/system/sink otherwise; U3 §5.9: a refused flag combination — with output_file, with push_to_modal, or glimpse.run with no server-side scope — raises BEFORE any handler work and returns the universal invalid_parameter_combination envelope), consumes the flag so handlers never see it, and runs the handler inside archive_operation_scope — include installs the augmented snapshot when the store has a visible record (byte-identical when none), fallback/none run on the live view carrying the decision for the gate and the miss texts. A fallback run whose gate requested it re-runs the handler EXACTLY once, augmented, reason 'automatic', corrections reset, first outcome (return or exception) discarded (§4.5).

duplicate_py.name: 🚨 Duplicate beacon ID (PY): fx@dup
duplicate_py.note:
This file contains multiple @beacon blocks with the same id.

Why this matters:
- F12 refresh matches nodes by beacon id.
- Duplicate ids create ambiguous matches and may cause reorder storms.

Fix:
- Make beacon ids unique (or correct @beacon-close blocks).
- Then press F12 again.
